An absent NPC, unavailable room, missing route, or old save produces a recoverable branch that explains which evidence is missing.

### Field 04 supplement — secondary stories with different stakes

**An Honest Distance** follows a courier who can only report that smoke was visible beyond a known landmark. The player’s job is to preserve the difference between “seen from here” and “confirmed at the site.” Its closing choice is about a careful map/archive note, not suppression.

**The Work That Can Wait** centers on the human cost of interrupting a useful repair. The player checks the existing project owner, hears what delay would affect, and chooses a limited pause or no action. If there is no current project schedule result, the story says the work crew has not reported one; it does not invent lost work units.

**Spare Coupling** follows one repair part from storage to an authorized job. The player sees its canonical inventory count and the destination’s need before confirming dispatch. The item is not a new wildfire resource; it is a normal item with normal ownership and the current item consumer remains authoritative.

**The Note After Rain** asks whether an old observation still describes current conditions. The player can request a fresh report through an existing communications path or preserve the old note with its date. It does not make rainfall a hidden fire-extinguishing simulation.

All four scenes can be told with a small number of existing characters only after character-index and quest-collision review. Names and voices remain unassigned in this plan to avoid silently adding people to faction canon.

### Field 05 supplement — recovery action catalogue

| Recovery action | Required proof | If proof is missing |
|---|---|---|
| Reopen the original work request | Current work owner accepts reopening | Keep it closed and explain |
| Return the suppression manifold | Inventory owner accepts transfer | Leave custody unresolved |
| Correct the site marker | Cartography owner accepts a real location reference | Preserve the uncertain note |
| Archive a witness statement | Archive intake confirms the record | Keep the original document with its owner |
| Send an all-clear | Incident owner reports closure and the channel owner accepts the message | Send a qualified update or no message |
| Resume a travel route | Travel owner confirms availability | Do not launch the next expedition |
| Publish an after-action note | Press/communications host returns a result | Retain as draft or private note |
| Clear a temporary instruction | The system that owns it accepts removal | Show that it remains active |

Every recovery row has a no-op state that preserves existing ownership. The plan should not build a single “restore area” button that performs all of them invisibly.

### Field 06 supplement — high-volume report variants

The report library can vary the evidence source while keeping the same small set of player verbs. Candidate variants include a direct worker note; a copied radio fragment; a late archive entry; a second-hand traveler account; a location correction request; a failed attempt to reach a work owner; a duplicate message; an old message with a known timestamp; a witnessed tool shutdown; an uncertain water request; an inventory mismatch; a return note from a halted journey; a print-run receipt without delivery confirmation; a seasonal forecast mention without a fire-state claim; and a “no observation” callback.

For each variant, the authoring record includes source identity, source certainty, source day, canonical location key, supporting owner, permitted action, all negative outcomes, and one sentence that explains what is still unknown. A validator should eventually catch blank source keys, references to missing locations/items, choice commands with no owner, duplicated quest IDs, invalid result text, and branches without closure. That future validation belongs to the current catalog/integrity owner; this plan does not add a private validator runner.

### Field 07 supplement — mechanical integration boundaries

The manifold can appear in three distinct states: carried by a party, present in canonical storage, or unavailable. Only the inventory and travel owners can change those states. The description that a manifold helps suppress sparks does not establish that it fights an active wildfire. If a future mechanics proposal adds a field-work action, it must identify whether the current item-consumer interface accepts a context-specific command and how the result is reported.

WeatherSystem and NuclearWinterProgressionSystem may provide context for authored text if their active host exposes the needed facts. Their existence does not imply that the fire proposal can read wind direction, fuel moisture, ignition probability, smoke exposure, or vegetation condition. No content record may add an effect field for these values until the source is inspected and the owning domain approves the coupling. Plan 158’s shelter disaster response stays scoped to its already integrated acute shelter incidents.

### Field 08 supplement — narrative voice and endings

There are four closure voices. The crew’s note is concrete and dated. A public notice uses restrained language and says what is confirmed. A private family callback is brief and does not convert loss into a reward meter. An archive summary states which sources remain unresolved. No ending congratulates the player for “defeating the fire” unless an owner has actually confirmed that outcome.

The three principal endings are **verified closure**, **protected work with no confirmed event**, and **record preserved under uncertainty**. A fourth ending, **request declined**, describes the owner’s refusal without marking the player as a failure. Any injury, property loss, ecological consequence, or damage to the shelter is authored only when an existing system creates and saves that consequence.

### Field 09 supplement — load profile and deterministic test scenarios

The proposed workload is event-based and bounded: at most one active report in the initial slice; at most one owner query per explicit inspection; at most one accepted dispatch action; one closure callback; and one optional archive or communication action. The UI must not poll route, weather, or work systems while idle. If the feature later grows to multiple concurrent reports, set an approved maximum, define stable sorting, and measure the peak before introducing any aggregate scan.

The replay workbook should cover the same command stream under fresh start and loaded save. Cases include: source verified; source contradicts itself; item missing; item delivered; dispatch declined; route unavailable; report repeated; player defers then returns; closure arrives before the panel opens; closure arrives while the panel is open; archive is unavailable; player cancels at confirmation; and restore occurs after a pending request. The output comparison is owner state and stable quest/receipt data, not presentation timing.

### Field 10 supplement — phase gates and budget discipline

**Gate 0 — evidence:** map exact use of the manifold and current outdoor travel/work commands. No content IDs are committed before this gate.

**Gate 1 — report-only narrative:** verify that a report can be presented and dismissed through an existing quest/event surface. This phase must not claim fire simulation.

**Gate 2 — one owner action:** wire one supported work or travel command, its owner result, refusal, and callback. Save ownership is recorded if state persists.

**Gate 3 — aftermath:** add one recovery action through an existing owner and demonstrate it survives close/reopen and save/restore.

**Gate 4 — volume:** add more sources/locations only after the first route is measured and content collision review passes.

Do not design a world-fire model in parallel with Gate 1. If reviewers decide that a spread simulation is necessary for the campaign’s promise, pause this plan and obtain a separate architecture owner, deterministic model contract, data authority, resource budget, save design, and focused replay plan. The writing cannot make missing simulation safe by using more dramatic prose.

## Pass 27 — Outdoor incident architecture decision record

This decision record prevents the word “wildland” from quietly turning into an unapproved world simulation. The game already has indoor shelter fire and acute shelter-disaster owners. Outdoor content can still offer a meaningful management story without modeling a moving firefront. A systemic simulation, by contrast, would be a new Core authority with weather, travel, work, inventory, map, and save implications. The integration foreman must choose the implementation shape after the outdoor owner census.

### Field 01 supplement — three implementation shapes

| Shape | Player promise | State needed | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Report-and-response narrative | Receive, verify, defer, communicate, and recover from a hazard report | Existing quest/event choice plus owner references | Preferred first exploration |
| Discrete outdoor incident | A known location has a confirmed incident phase and supported response commands | New or explicitly extended incident state with save ownership | Not approved; exact no-duplicate premise required |
| Propagating firefront | Fire changes spatially over time and affects routes, jobs, or ecology | Deterministic simulation, authored inputs, migrations, and measured performance | Requires separate architecture decision |

Shape B is not an innocuous compromise: even one persistent incident can become a second truth for access or severity. Shape C cannot be introduced through item descriptions, map cards, or a panel callback. If the census finds a current outdoor hazard owner, extend it and reject these shapes unless an exact remaining gap is proven.

### Field 02 supplement — boundary contract

The report owns only its text and source references. The quest/event owner owns acknowledgement. The work owner owns whether a job stops or restarts. Inventory owns the manifold and all carried supplies. Travel owns whether a journey can be dispatched or completed. Cartography owns place identity. Communications or the press owner owns the message result. ShelterArchiveSystem owns any accepted historical record. A future approved outdoor incident owner may report incident facts, but it does not take over these neighboring concerns.

The panel composes read-only facts and sends one command to one owner. Cross-owner transactions must have an existing host transaction or an explicit event sequence. Where no transaction exists, show partial success and a recovery action; do not display atomic success because the narrative sequence expects it.

### Field 03 supplement — candidate incident vocabulary

If Shape B is approved, the eventual owner may need concepts such as *reported*, *verified*, *response requested*, *response accepted*, *closed*, and *unknown*. These are design terms, not final enum values. The owner must decide whether “verified” is incident phase or evidence quality. “Accepted” means an owner accepted a command, not that the outcome is guaranteed. “Closed” means the incident owner confirms closure, not that all recovery work is finished.

Candidate authored references are a stable scene key, canonical location, source reference, observed time from the existing campaign clock, evidence category, current owner response, closure reference, and data-version authority. Severity, spread rate, smoke exposure, wind, and burn condition are omitted until an existing or newly approved domain owner defines their semantics and save behavior. A convenient `fireLevel` float in JSON is not a substitute.

### Field 04 supplement — candidate incident records

| Draft scene key | Only defensible initial fact | Required source response | Honest closure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `candidate_mile_shift_note` | Late note mentions smoke near a work site | Work/location owner confirms current condition | Note corrected or left unresolved |
| `candidate_ash_marker` | Traveler says a marker is obscured | Cartography resolves its canonical identity | Map corrected or caveated |
| `candidate_grinding_stop` | Worker says equipment may be off | Work owner returns current status | Work open, closed, or unknown |
| `candidate_return_manifest` | A trip was requested | Travel owner returns accepted/completed/refused | Dispatch described accurately |
| `candidate_manifold_check` | Item may be present | Inventory confirms custody | Transfer completed or declined |
| `candidate_old_witness` | An observation occurred in the past | Archive/source supplies provenance | Old evidence retained as old |
| `candidate_no_signal` | No reply has arrived | Communications returns pending/unavailable | Story closes without a claim |
| `candidate_public_correction` | Public copy may be stale | Press route confirms actual publication | New copy printed or held |

These keys are authoring placeholders and must not enter production data. Any owner query can reject a candidate before prose is expanded.

### Field 05 supplement — three first-season story blueprints

**The Tools Went Quiet** follows a shift transition. The player compares a worker’s direct account with the current work receipt and decides whether to pause the next crew or request supported inspection. The callback says whether work was actually paused. Recovery is tool custody and a truthful handover, not a firefighting minigame.

**The Marker Has No Back** follows a damaged place label. The player has a current map reference and an old handwritten copy, but no verified direction from the witness. They can submit a correction with source, preserve the historic label, or decline to direct travel. Cartography owns the map result; only the travel owner decides whether the route is usable.

**The Spare Line** features the existing Water Spark Suppression Manifold. A work party asks to use it before grinding resumes. The player checks whether that exact item has an active consumer and whether the work owner accepts the operation. If either is false, the story does not imply that the manifold prevented a fire. A transfer story is allowed only if the current inventory owner supports it.

### Field 06 supplement — recovery actions and proof

| Recovery action | Proof required | Missing-proof behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Reopen a work request | Work owner accepts reopening | Keep it closed and explain |
| Return the manifold | Inventory accepts transfer | Leave custody unresolved |
| Correct a site marker | Cartography accepts canonical location | Preserve uncertain note |
| Archive witness statement | Archive intake confirms record | Keep original with its holder |
| Send an all-clear | Incident closure and channel acceptance | Send qualified update or none |
| Resume travel | Travel owner confirms route | Do not launch next trip |
| Publish after-action note | Press/communications returns result | Retain draft or private note |
| Clear temporary instruction | Owning system accepts removal | Show instruction remains active |

There is no one-click “restore area” action; each owner changes only the state it owns. A recovery branch can complete by preserving a factual unknown result.

### Field 07 supplement — strategic tradeoff

The player weighs interruption of productive work, use of an available response, and waiting until evidence improves. A decision affects a real schedule only if the work owner supplies that state and accepts the change. If no schedule exists, portray the conflict through testimony, not a fabricated lost-day total. Scarcity comes from canonical inventory and labor owners; there is no fire currency.

Weather or winter systems may supply context only where the active host exposes the fact. Their existence does not prove the availability of wind direction, fuel moisture, ignition chance, smoke exposure, or vegetation condition. Plan 158’s shelter response remains scoped to the integrated shelter incidents.

### Field 08 supplement — clear observation and consequence

Players must distinguish witness assertion, owner result, player interpretation, and authored context. A source label such as “direct,” “copied,” “unconfirmed,” or “contradictory” is sufficient unless a current owner already exposes a scale. Before a command, show the exact action and cost. After it, replace the prediction with the actual owner result. Opening a report cannot itself trigger an emergency, move a worker, spend an item, or close a route.

The principal endings are verified closure, protected work with no confirmed event, record preserved under uncertainty, and owner refusal. None congratulates the player for defeating a fire unless an owner confirms that outcome. Injury, property loss, ecological consequence, and damage are authored only when an existing system produces and saves them.

### Field 09 supplement — system budget and replay envelope

The first slice has no per-frame computation or daily incident scan. It loads one report, queries one owner per explicit inspection, issues at most one accepted action, and uses one closure callback. A later multi-incident scope needs a fixed cap, stable sort, bounded active state, and a peak measurement.

If a new simulation is approved, its brief must define tick rate, max locations, deterministic order, numeric method, RNG stream if required, event production, save format, migration, and benchmark. It must also show how travel, work, and map owners consume output and what happens when output is missing. Time comes from the current simulation clock; dictionary order and wall-clock time cannot define spread. Randomness must obey the existing seeded RNG contract.

### Field 10 supplement — handoff and decision result

The implementation dossier records exact files, claim dependencies, chosen shape, source/data references, current owner methods/events, state written, save section, supported actions, unknown/refusal handling, UI route, collision review, performance envelope, and focused verification. A normal build must reach one successful route and one refusal/unknown route.

The feature remains DRAFT until this evidence exists. If the verified slice is content-only, call it an incident-report story, not a firefront system. If it needs a new simulation authority, pause for the architecture decision before any story claims a mechanical outcome.

## Pass 28 — Burn-recovery decisions after incident closure

Recovery begins only after the current incident/work owner returns a closure fact. This section adds a second kind of play to the expansion: stewardship after the urgent report, where the player chooses which truthful records and existing work requests deserve attention next. It does not simulate ecological succession, soil damage, smoke, or regrowth. The game already has weather and seasonal progression owners that may provide context, but none of that establishes a burn-ecology authority.

### Field 01 supplement — closure is the start of recovery, not a victory flag

The post-incident screen preserves the distinction between “no incident confirmed,” “owner reports contained/closed,” “work remains paused,” and “recovery request accepted.” These states must not collapse into a universal green check. If closure is only narrative, the interface labels it as a report. If the work owner still shows a task open, recovery cannot silently reopen or mark it done.

The player can choose one follow-up: restore a supported work task, investigate a map/archive discrepancy, carry a supply receipt, publish a qualified notice, or leave the site alone. These options can have different logistical or social consequences only through their owners. The player is allowed to decide that there is not enough evidence for more action.

### Field 02 supplement — recovery owner map

| Candidate recovery fact | Possible existing owner | Promotion rule |
|---|---|---|
| Site identity or marker condition | CartographySystem | Use its canonical location and accepted correction result |
| Project or work status | ColonySystem or current work owner | Read/issue only supported project commands |
| Shelter room state | ShelterExpansionSystem/room owner | Do not turn outdoor damage into room damage |
| Current weather/season context | Weather and NuclearWinterProgression owners | Display only values actually exposed to the active host |
| Material custody | Canonical inventory | Use actual transfer receipt and amount |
| Event scheduling | SeasonalCelebrationSystem | Reuse current event; no new restoration calendar |
| Historical incident note | ShelterArchiveSystem | Intake and provenance must be supported |
| Public correction | Existing communications or press host | Distinguish draft, print, and reach |

An absent owner row remains a design blocker. It is not acceptable to create “land condition” in this feature because that term sounds useful. If no ecological owner exists, the recovery episode stays about work, records, and people.

### Field 03 supplement — restoration request scope

A recovery request states a source, canonical location, bounded concern, supporting evidence, proposed existing action, and uncertainty. It avoids invented numerical severity. “The marker is unreadable in the submitted note” can be checked against CartographySystem; “the site is 63% burned” cannot appear without a defined measure owner. “The crew has not received a new work order” can be verified through the project source; “the land is unusable” cannot be inferred from a burn story.

The player preview distinguishes any cost or irreversible action. Existing stock is checked at commitment. If a project consumes material, the inventory owner confirms the transfer. If a route changes, travel/map owners confirm it. If the only result is an accepted document, the player is told that the outcome is documentary.

### Field 04 supplement — recovery chapter “What We Can Put Back”

In the opening, the player receives a confirmed work closure or a qualified report that activity stopped. A worker asks whether the site may be used again, but the current route state is unavailable. The player can request a supported inspection, return a piece of equipment to storage, or leave an observation with its source. Each is a separate current-owner action.

In the middle, a replacement work request arrives with a location name taken from an old note. Cartography and the archive report different dates. The player can request a current label, preserve the historical note, or postpone the request until its destination resolves. Nothing claims that the fire changed the map.

At the close, an existing project owner accepts or refuses a new scope. If it accepts, the story follows the owner’s result. If it refuses, the player may retain the request or communicate the refusal. If no owner responds, the story ends with the open question. The arc is complete when the player makes a supported decision and receives an accurate callback, not when land returns to an invented ideal state.

### Field 05 supplement — recovery task cards

| Card | Player action | Required callback |
|---|---|---|
| Return the Tool | Transfer the existing item through Inventory | Transfer receipt or refusal |
| Correct the Marker | Submit exact location through CartographySystem | Accepted label or unresolved source |
| Reopen the Shift | Ask work owner to accept a new task | Accepted/declined task state |
| Copy the Closure | Request a record through archive/communications | Intake or delivery result |
| Keep Both Dates | Preserve old and current place references | Archive/map citation |
| Ask Before Dispatch | Check current route through travel owner | Available or unavailable result |
| Hold the Notice | Keep a public claim unsent pending proof | Draft remains a draft |
| Report No Change | Close with owner’s unchanged status | Explicit unchanged callback |
| Give the Crew Its Receipt | Return accepted work evidence | Existing request owner acknowledges |
| Leave the Site Quiet | Decline further action | No consequence is invented |

These tasks provide repeatable play without an artificial cleanup meter. A completed task does not imply that all damage is repaired.

### Field 06 supplement — restoration story variants

**The Place Left Off the Map** follows a site that does not resolve in the current canonical map. The player can avoid dispatch, request correction through the map owner, or preserve the author’s note without directing travel. The player is not rewarded for guessing.

**The Replacement Handle** concerns one existing tool that can be repaired, borrowed, or left in place only if the canonical inventory/work owners support those states. The story is about who can continue the accepted work, not a new equipment durability system.

**A Notice After Closure** asks what the community should hear once an owner closes a report. The player may share confirmed facts, share a qualified report, or keep the source private. The communication owner returns the actual send/print result. No reach number is fabricated.

### Field 07 supplement — seasonal callbacks without an ecology simulation

Seasonal content can change a scene’s context if NuclearWinterProgressionSystem or SeasonalCelebrationSystem exposes the phase/event. A callback may say that a work request is being considered during the current season; it cannot derive a new travel penalty, growth cycle, plant list, heating cost, or burn severity from the season. Those consequences belong to existing owners or require a distinct signed system proposal.

Later scenes should be triggered by owner events rather than fixed days. This lets a player finish or defer the chapter without an artificial timer. If no callback event is available, an optional journal/quest revisit is acceptable only through a current route that already supports it. The plan must not create a recurring notification.

### Field 08 supplement — map/notice/record storytelling

Recovery stories preserve provenance as a mechanic: who saw the site, when, how directly, and which owner confirmed it. The player can select a formal notice, private callback, or no publication. The content explains that a map correction changes the present reference while an archive note preserves an earlier claim. Neither makes the old witness dishonest.

If a published line is later corrected, the original must remain visible if the press/archive owner supports history. If not, the writer must not imply a permanent public paper trail. The result screen can still say “new copy accepted; prior reach unknown.”

### Field 09 supplement — performance and persistence after closure

The recovery UI loads one closed incident’s source references and current owner states on demand. It does not scan all historical reports or continuously query every location. Archive search is user-initiated; map, work, and inventory states update only through their own signals. Closing the panel releases listeners. A reopened report queries current values and clearly marks changed facts.

Incident closure and recovery progress remain separate save facts only if their current owners already store them. If the report exists solely in a quest state, its callback uses that state. If a new persistent recovery task is required, request owner assignment before adding a save field. The save test covers a completed incident with a pending recovery request, a declined request, a deleted content reference, and a restored owner result.

### Field 10 supplement — accepted recovery tranche

The first recovery add-on should contain one closure callback, two supported follow-up actions, one map/archive story variant, and a clear no-action ending. Any second or third location waits until the canonical place IDs and owner APIs are verified. The authoring group reports environmental systems intentionally untouched, especially vegetation, soil, smoke, and water.

The tranche is complete only when the player can move from owner-confirmed closure into one real follow-up, observe its true result, and reopen the story without a duplicate command. This expansion’s recovery promise is accountable continuity: a place, a request, and a record remain truthful after the emergency story ends.

## Pass 29 — Incident edge-case workbook and command truth table

This final packet exercises the report/owner boundary under the cases most likely to create a false emergency, duplicate action, or impossible recovery. It is an implementation review aid for a future vertical slice. The cases do not assert that any outdoor command currently exists.

### Field 01 supplement — report identity and duplicate handling

Every external or authored report must have a stable source reference from its owner. The content key identifies text; it is not sufficient to deduplicate live events. A repeated radio message, repeated witness dialog, and repeated archive search can all refer to the same event. If the current event/quest owner already deduplicates those sources, reuse that behavior. If no stable event identity is exposed, present the report as repeated information but do not issue a second work or inventory command.

If two reports contradict each other, the UI keeps their source and time separate. It does not average them into a new certainty number or choose whichever arrived last. A report from an old save whose location ID no longer resolves remains a historical note; the game does not redirect it to the nearest location.

### Field 02 supplement — command truth table

| Player action | Precondition to show enabled | Result that changes UI | Retry behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inspect report | Report reference is readable | Evidence/source details open | Reopen is read-only |
| Request verification | Current source owner accepts query | Owner returns confirmed/unknown/unavailable | Explicit retry only if supported |
| Halt work | Current work owner exposes and accepts command | Work result reports accepted/refused | Do not resend after accepted |
| Transfer manifold | Inventory and target owner support transfer | Transfer receipt updates custody | Recheck quantity before retry |
| Dispatch party | Travel owner resolves canonical route | Accepted/completed/refused response | Never infer arrival from acceptance |
| Correct marker | Canonical place key resolves | Cartography returns accepted correction | New correction is a new request |
| Publish update | Current host supports a real publication | Press/communication result | Draft is not a sent run |
| Archive note | Current archive intake supports the record | Intake receipt or refusal | Preserve original on rejection |

If the precondition is false or unknown, render the action disabled with an explanation only when the owner can supply one. A generic error does not become a new gameplay state.

### Field 03 supplement — failure and recovery matrix

| Failure or interruption | State that must remain authoritative | Player-facing recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Report arrives after owner already closed | Current closure result | Show late report as history |
| Same report is opened twice | Existing event identity | No duplicate command |
| Item was consumed elsewhere after preview | Current inventory | Re-preview or cancel; never go negative locally |
| Route is unavailable after briefing | Travel owner | Cancel before dispatch or show accepted limits |
| Panel closes during pending command | Command owner | Re-query on reopen; do not resubmit |
| Save loads without old location | Map/save owner | Keep historical text unresolved |
| Witness becomes unavailable | Roster/dialogue owner | Close with source unavailable |
| Press host is absent | Current communication route | Keep draft; do not show printed copies |
| Archive declines source | Archive owner | Return original to holder if supported |
| Owner sends same callback twice | Owner event identity | Idempotent display and no repeated effect |
| Player chooses no action | No owner mutation | Close as a valid defer/no-action branch |
| Current data version removes a scene | Approved content migration | Close/quarantine through owner policy |

### Field 04 supplement — report copy status rules

The incident journal uses plain status words: *reported* means a source sent a claim; *checked* means an owner returned a verification result; *requested* means the player issued an action; *accepted* means an owner accepted that action; *complete* means that owner returned a completion; and *unknown* means no trustworthy answer arrived. The words are not interchangeable. A translated string must preserve the distinction.

When a status changes, the previous report and source remain discoverable if the owning log/archive supports history. If it does not, the panel shows a small current history in quest state only when the selected quest owner already persists it. No second audit log is created for narrative convenience.

### Field 05 supplement — no-response ending in detail

The no-response ending is not a failure animation. It says which source did not respond if known, whether the player has an action that can safely be taken without that response, and whether the request remains pending according to its owner. If no pending state exists, the story closes with “not confirmed” rather than retaining an orphaned active entry. The player may keep a report card in a current journal/archive route only if it supports that record.

The closing prose acknowledges the cost of waiting without implying a hidden damage outcome: a crew cannot be told that it is safe, the player cannot claim that work resumed, and the report remains available for later verification if a current event provides it. The player receives a useful conclusion—what is known and what can be done—without a fabricated answer.

### Field 06 supplement — environmental and logistical unknowns

Fire direction, spread speed, burn radius, heat, air quality, water exposure, soil condition, tree loss, animal movement, crop effect, and route safety remain outside this first feature unless a current owner exposes them. A scene can include a witness description such as “the smoke seemed farther east” only as a witnessed impression with time/source. It cannot affect current travel or hazard values.

The Wildland plan’s eventual simulation proposal must separately address deterministic input capture and gameplay consequence. Weather today cannot be applied retroactively to yesterday’s report without a stored observation from its owner. A location’s current map label cannot establish historical burn geometry. A picture or prose line is not simulation evidence.

### Field 07 supplement — late consequence and debrief

The debrief answers four questions: What did the player hear? Which owner did they query? What command did they issue or decline? Which result was confirmed? It can show a fifth line, “what remains uncertain,” but cannot total casualties or ecological impact without current owners. A late event may add one short callback if the quest owner records a stable closure reference.

Achievement and ending hooks, if desired, route to their current owners and use objective evidence already available. A new award for “all fire outcomes” would require an existing achievement definition and real measurable criteria; this plan does not invent an achievement or use completion count as fire statistics.

### Field 08 supplement — accessible incident log behavior

The log can be read linearly by screen reader, with date, source, statement, owner check, and result spoken in that order. Table headings are repeated as labels on narrow display layouts. Contradictory sources are not distinguished only by red/green. Focus returns to the selected report after details close. A pending result announces once when the player opens the report or when a real owner state-change signal arrives; no repeated alert loop runs.

### Field 09 supplement — focused acceptance scenario sequence

An eventual package owner may use this bounded scenario sequence: start with a stale report; open it twice; request one current owner check; cancel before any action; reload; open the same report; revalidate; confirm an accepted work command; receive a delayed refusal or completion; close; reopen; and verify no duplicate order or item transfer. A parallel scenario uses contradictory sources and ends unresolved. Verification belongs to the active package’s focused target and the current Godot route; this document does not authorize a broad test run.

### Field 10 supplement — final stop/go review

Proceed with a report-only story if content is reachable but no outdoor simulation exists. Proceed with one owner action if its consumer, callback, and persistence are proven. Stop if the feature needs a second route state, an unowned environment value, or a hidden copy of another system’s save data. Escalate a new simulation request with measurable runtime bounds and a single authoritative owner.

That stop/go result should appear at the top of the eventual implementation ticket, so a later author does not mistake a large plan for approval. The feature is only as broad as the owner route and evidence actually support.

## Pass 30 — Wildland incident evidence, bounded response, and recovery tranches

This pass converts the firefront idea into a source-aware feature package that can remain useful even if no landscape-fire simulation is approved. The current weather cascade owns location access closures and expedition travel delays; the disaster-response authority covers acute shelter crises, including electrical fire. A wildland front, a shelter fire, a weather closure, and a rumor about smoke are separate facts. This plan adds no second closure table, shelter protocol, or unowned daily fire tick.

### Field 01 supplement — Proposal boundary and present owners

The first deliverable is a player-legible incident dossier, not a new map simulation. It assembles dated observations and references supplied by existing owners: a weather forecast, an access result, an expedition report, an inventory inspection, a faction statement, or an archive entry. Each input is labeled with its source and observation time. If no current API exposes a fact, the dossier says “not checked” rather than fabricating a proxy from a similarly named field.

The plan proposes an owner decision only after a package audit identifies a real command that can be issued now. Candidate decisions include postponing a dispatch through the existing route owner, documenting a suspected hazard, or allocating an existing item through its normal inventory consumer. The dossier cannot set a location closed, alter route distance, create smoke exposure, damage a structure, or grant a fireproofing bonus. Those actions require explicit ownership and a signed scope decision.

This boundary leaves a useful content outcome in every implementation case. A report-only release can deliver investigation, uncertainty, source comparison, and a narrative resolution. A later, separately approved simulation can enrich the same episode with stateful spread and recovery. Content identity must not silently change meaning when that later layer arrives.

### Field 02 supplement — Observation record and source confidence

Each observation row should contain a stable content ID, source owner, source reference, observed day or event time, reporter identity when known, canonical place reference when known, statement text key, and a confidence label explained in plain language. Confidence is not a universal numerical truth score. “Confirmed” means a current owner returned that fact; “corroborated” means two independent sources agree; “reported” means one source said it; “disputed” means an incompatible source exists; and “unknown” means the query did not establish an answer.

Deduplication must use source identity plus event identity, not matching prose. Two survivors repeating one rumor are one chain unless the source graph proves independent observation. A reopened dossier may refresh a live owner projection but must not rewrite a historical statement as if the speaker had known the future. Corrections append through the owning archive contract; they do not erase an earlier witness account.

Authored data references existing entity IDs and text keys. A row with an unresolved region, faction, item, or location ID stays in the design backlog. It must not be made “valid” by inventing a parallel alias registry. The integrity validator should distinguish malformed references, unavailable-at-runtime owners, and deliberately narrative-only content.

### Field 03 supplement — Weather and route interaction without a second closure owner

When an episode concerns weather, the current weather cascade is the authority for access and travel effects. The dossier may display its result with source and freshness, but cannot calculate a replacement threshold from rain, wind, or season. An episode can ask the player to compare a forecast with a field report; it cannot claim that a route is safe because its local weather score falls below a new cutoff.

If the player viewed a location yesterday and a current query now says access is restricted, the interface shows both the earlier note and the newer result. It says the owner’s present status supersedes the older projection for dispatch purposes. If a query fails, the route remains in the state returned by its canonical owner; failure to read status is never permission to dispatch.

Content can create tension without inventing mechanics. One report may describe a road visible from a ridge, while the owner’s travel result reflects a closure elsewhere on that route. Another may arrive too late to authorize immediate travel but remain useful for identifying a witness. These distinctions make investigation playable while respecting the actual access contract.

### Field 04 supplement — Distinct consequences and the architecture gate

Landscape burn, habitat change, ash deposition, and smoke exposure are attractive feature areas, but current evidence does not establish a single owner for them. The plan divides them into a narrative evidence layer and a possible future simulation package. The evidence layer may record observations and ask the player to preserve or compare them. It cannot decrement wildlife, modify crop yield, apply illness, change soil fertility, or set a region’s burned state.

Before simulation work is proposed, an integrator must answer: which world authority owns spatial extent; how a fire event is created and advanced; how deterministic seed use is assigned; which existing weather or expedition state is consumed; which systems receive consequences; and who captures and restores the event. The decision specifies scale, maximum concurrent incidents, update cadence, and bounded work per campaign day. If the solution needs a new map graph, cell ownership, or persisted ecology ledger, stop for an architecture decision instead of adding it as “content.”

Writers can prepare a conditional consequence matrix: observed, confirmed by owner, or future simulation only. This lets copy avoid overstating outcomes before implementation and protects a later feature from having to preserve prose that asserted spread through an unmodeled location.

### Field 05 supplement — Response choices using present commands

An episode offers only actions that reach a current command handler. “Review report,” “compare source,” and “decline action” are safe information choices. A dispatch choice appears only if the existing travel route accepts that destination and exposes a refusal outcome. An item-use choice appears only if a current item consumer exists for that context. `item_spark_suppression_manifold` remains a lead for inspection; its name does not prove an outdoor-fire action.

Each proposed choice needs a precondition table: required source facts, current owner queried, resources charged by that owner, expected callback or result, cancellation behavior, and save behavior. A design-time choice without an operational command can remain dialogue, but its result must be narrative-only and cannot imply that the player extinguished a front, protected a building, or treated a survivor.

Failure is an outcome rather than a hidden penalty. A route refusal carries the owner’s stated reason when available. If the owner cannot answer, the report remains unresolved. If a resource is unavailable, the UI identifies the authoritative inventory result, avoids double-charging, and returns focus to the same episode. Retrying must not duplicate an order or consume supplies twice.

### Field 06 supplement — Three connected story arcs

**The Black Line** begins with two conflicting field sketches. A surveyor marks a charred strip across an old boundary; a courier insists the smoke was from a controlled burn years ago. The player can request a current access result, compare the sketches with an archive record, or close the report as unverified. A later note reveals that the surveyor copied an obsolete map legend. The resolution rewards accurate documentation and careful refusal, not a hidden firefighting stat.

**The Orchard Register** follows a caretaker who reports that a slope has “gone quiet.” The first report is ambiguous: it may mean burned trees, seasonal dormancy, or abandoned work. A second witness identifies an old orchard marker. If a current cartography or wildlife owner returns a matching fact, the story may cite it; otherwise, the player receives a human account and no ecological state change. A side episode asks whether to preserve the caretaker’s spelling and local place-name when the official index uses another label. Both can be archived as source text while only canonical IDs drive gameplay.

**Smoke at the Door** concerns an anxious shelter resident who mistakes an electrical incident for a distant landscape fire. The shelter disaster owner decides whether an acute shelter crisis exists. The firefront dossier may help establish what was heard outside, but it cannot launch a second internal-fire protocol. The resolution teaches the difference between alarm, observation, and verified incident; it does not penalize the resident for seeking help.

Together these arcs provide investigation, a local-history side story, and an onboarding episode. Their common connective tissue is evidence handling. None requires landscape spread simulation, and each remains coherent if a future owner later supplies additional facts.

### Field 07 supplement — Quest packaging and reachable endings

Draft against the currently reachable quest owner only after its live catalog shape and host route are rechecked. Do not assume a general scenario browser, free-form prerequisite evaluator, or arbitrary branch set exists. Where the current quest contract permits a bounded objective sequence and a binary crisis decision, encode the episode in that shape. Otherwise keep it as a content packet pending an approved route.

Each arc has a minimum completion path and an optional evidence path. The minimum path closes with a truthful status such as verified, disproved, or unresolved. The optional path adds a second witness or archive citation, but does not require a new world-state variable merely to show that the player read a document. Persistent consequences must be a current owner’s result or a narrowly approved quest flag with an existing save owner.

Ending text is conditional on returned facts. “The road remains closed” appears only if the access owner says so when rendered. “The fire has passed” is unacceptable unless a world owner returned that event. Safer copy can state: “No active report confirms a front here; the earlier witness account remains in the archive.” This closes the investigation without pretending to close a simulation.

### Field 08 supplement — UX for reports, uncertainty, and fatigue

The incident view begins with one sentence describing what is known, followed by a short source list and freshness markers. The primary action is never styled as the default irreversible decision while sources are disputed. Source details reveal the original statement, timestamp, and owner; a compact summary preserves uncertainty instead of converting it to a green “safe” badge.

Keyboard and controller users traverse source → statement → current owner result → actions → outcome. Focus returns to the originating report after details close. A failed lookup has a stable retry control and plain explanation. Repeated opening does not replay an alert or append duplicate archive records. Screen-reader output names source and date before statement; confidence uses text and iconography, not color alone.

Reports need a quiet mode. New evidence can use an existing notification or quest surface if that route supports it; this plan adds no parallel inbox. Audio cues use the current accessibility owner’s visual-notification and alert-coalescing behavior when available. The report remains readable with optional sound disabled.

### Field 09 supplement — Bounded cost and save contract

The report surface loads a small, selected set of evidence references. It must not scan every expedition, map, journal, rumor, and archive entry on every frame. The player opens a dossier on demand; owner reads happen on open or explicit refresh. The view subscribes only while visible and releases listeners on close, scene exit, campaign load, or owner disposal.

Persisted state is limited to what the existing quest or archive owner already records. A report cache is a disposable projection keyed by source reference and freshness, not a second save store. A future simulation’s incident state belongs to its assigned world owner and needs deterministic initialization, capture, restore, migration/default behavior, and paired replay acceptance. Wall-clock time and unordered collection order cannot influence a fire outcome.

Performance acceptance measures worst-case open time with a large archive, repeat-open allocation growth, and close/reopen listener count. If a content pack adds many reports, lazy indexing and paging are preferable to eager construction of a global witness graph. The report remains responsive when an optional source is retired or cannot load.

### Field 10 supplement — Release tranche and evidence review

Tranche A is content-only: three story arcs, source IDs, text keys, uncertainty labels, and accessibility copy. Tranche B is a report route only if an existing player-facing owner can present and close it without new state. Tranche C is one existing command binding, limited to a current travel, inventory, archive, or quest seam proven by the package audit. Tranche D, landscape spread or ecological consequence, is a separate architecture decision and implementation package.

Reviewers challenge each verb in the copy: does the player observe, request, dispatch, treat, suppress, or merely record? Each verb must match an owner result. The acceptance review samples stale evidence, contradictory witnesses, an unavailable location, no matching item consumer, route refusal, reload, controller navigation, and a report reopened after the world has changed.

If an accepted ending claims a consequence that no current system owns, the package returns to content revision. If results remain accurate and a player can close an unresolved incident without penalty, the report-only tranche can ship as a complete investigative story while the larger simulation waits for its own evidence and authority.

## Pass 31 — Winter-weather evidence web and recovery-content tranche

This pass expands the report-first design around current environmental authorities that were recently integrated: nuclear-winter phase and season progression, weather gameplay cascades, map discovery, and shelter disaster response. Those systems provide better facts for a wildland story, but they still do not prove a landscape-fire owner. The intended result is a richer, cross-system incident and stewardship experience that reads the actual owners without simulating the same condition twice.

### Field 01 expansion — A new player loop from forecast to stewardship

The player loop is split into four clocks that the UI never collapses into one “fire danger” meter. The climate phase is a long-horizon world condition returned by the winter progression owner. The current weather forecast or evaluated cascade is a nearer-horizon condition. The location-access result answers whether an existing travel route is usable. The fire dossier contains reports and observations, which may be stale or disputed. A player first learns which clock each statement belongs to, then makes a choice appropriate to that clock.

An episode can now create layered decisions without introducing a new simulation. Before a trip, a player may compare a forecast to the current access projection. During a follow-up, the player may preserve a witness statement and mark the location as not yet surveyed. After the immediate concern, the player may decide whether to keep an observation in an existing archive. These actions have distinct outcomes: route decision, evidence provenance, and historical record. None changes climate or ecology.

The loop should remain playable when one source is missing. If weather has no current forecast for the cited location, the player can still hear the witness and document the uncertainty. If CartographySystem does not expose a matching region, a locally named place remains quoted text without gameplay ID. If the archive cannot accept the record, the quest can still resolve in-session and report that durable filing is unavailable. No source failure silently blocks the main story.

### Field 02 expansion — Environmental fact hierarchy and trigger rules

The event packet consumes information in a strict hierarchy. First, current owner facts: current phase, season, weather effects, route-access state, discovered region, and active shelter emergency if the corresponding owner exposes each one. Second, time-stamped world observations: a report, sketch, or recovered item. Third, authored context: dialogue and archive excerpts. Authored context cannot override a current owner result. A test scenario’s expected value cannot be treated as live campaign state.

Every trigger used in production must be one of three kinds: an explicit owner event already emitted; a player command that asks an owner for current state; or a static narrative prerequisite supported by the active quest contract. “When smoke is high,” “after three dry days,” and “when the hillside burns” are not valid trigger labels until an owner exposes those measurements and thresholds. This distinction keeps content writers from building dependencies on attractive but nonexistent telemetry.

The environmental crosswalk should list owner, read contract, result timestamp, stale policy, failure behavior, and whether the fact may be persisted by the dossier. Read contracts are projections. The dossier may retain a quoted historical source if the quest/archive contract permits it, but it never snapshots mutable weather or access state into a competing save section.

### Field 03 expansion — New data families and validation rules

The content tranche adds four small, reference-driven data families rather than one broad event database. `fire_observation_sources` identifies speaker or artifact source and provenance. `fire_dossier_entries` points to owner facts and story text keys. `recovery_conversations` binds follow-up dialogue to a returned outcome category. `stewardship_actions` lists which existing action surface is offered and the exact owner command, if any. These are proposed authoring names only; an implementation package must adapt to the current data-authority conventions before creating files.

Each row carries a stable snake_case ID, schema version, localization keys, canonical references, source age policy, confidence vocabulary, and a `content_only` or `owner_bound` marker. `owner_bound` rows require a current consumer; data validation reports rows whose owner is absent. `content_only` is not a hidden fallback that awards state. It explicitly tells the runtime and reviewer that the content can close narratively without claiming a world mutation.

The validator should reject a row that refers to both a stale owner snapshot and a current command result as if they were interchangeable; a row that cites a destroyed or unknown map ID; a publication reference with no print-result identity; a consequence with no owner; duplicate source/event pairs; unreachable branch keys; and any unlocalized long-form text. It should also warn when a story calls a reported observation “confirmed.” A row-level report makes the future content pack auditable without loading the full campaign catalog in the runtime.

### Field 04 expansion — Four owner-aware story arcs

**The Pale Marker** starts during a late winter phase when the daylight projection changes. A surveyor finds a white marker above a route that has never been mapped by the shelter. The player can preserve the marker’s inscription, ask for a current scouting route if the map and expedition owners support it, or close the matter as local testimony. The story never assumes that less daylight caused a fire; it uses the climate facts to explain why the team’s observation window differs from the old notebook.

**After the Access Notice** begins when a delayed courier returns with a warning that appears to contradict a current location-access result. The player compares the message time to the present cascade result and chooses whether to print, archive, or leave the warning uncirculated. If a publication command is available, the Press engine owns its run and audience estimate. This remains a wildland report story; it does not duplicate the community-work project that owns a repair order.

**The Unlit Window** follows a shelter resident who repeatedly reports distant light during the “ash summer” season. Existing DisasterResponseSystem governs acute internal crises; the dossier can ask the player to request the shelter owner’s current incident state before opening a landscape investigation. If there is no incident, the narrative resolves the fear respectfully. If a real crisis is returned, the regular emergency route takes precedence and the dossier closes as secondary context.

**Three Names for One Slope** follows a cartographer, an elder, and a traveler who use three names for a single location. CartographySystem determines the canonical discovered region and POI, while the quotations remain attached to their actual speakers. The final decision may preserve multiple names in text or use the canonical label on a map projection; it never registers three copies of the location.

Each arc supports a low-dependency version and an owner-enriched version. The low-dependency version relies on testimony and static source material. The enriched version adds a current owner result when available. Both versions share the same character resolution so that build configuration does not change canon.

### Field 05 expansion — Recovery card bank with explicit evidence classes

The high-volume authoring pack contains 24 recovery cards divided by what is known, not by an invented damage tier: six confirmed-owner updates; six witness-only accounts; four conflicting-source cases; four obsolete-map or stale-message cases; and four unresolved references. Each card contains a short opening, one source question, one optional follow-up, a close condition, and a sentence that states what remains unknown. Repetition is reduced through distinct speakers, delivery media, and stakes rather than different adjectives for the same observation.

Example cards include a melted trail marker whose age cannot be established; a charred cooking pit mistaken for a brushfire remnant; a map that labels an abandoned track as a road; a blanket of ash described by one traveler but absent from the current survey; a damaged relay that delivered a message after its author left; and a caretaker who asks that a family path not be turned into a public route. These are content leads, not assertions about current simulation. Their card metadata requires a reviewer to mark every claim as owner-confirmed, source-reported, author-context, or future-simulation-only.

Side outcomes add practical variety: preserve an oral history, return a map copy, correct a dated notice, ask the cartographer to append a note, or decline circulation. None awards resource items unless an existing catalog row and command support it. A social response can be a dialogue change or quest ending, but any morale, trust, faction, or reputation mutation must be returned by a current owner and recorded once.

### Field 06 expansion — Cross-owner handshake and failure isolation

The handshake table for the first package is intentionally small. WeatherSystem and its cascade may answer forecast/effect/access questions. NuclearWinterProgressionSystem may answer phase and seasonal context. CartographySystem may answer discovered map state. DisasterResponseSystem may answer active shelter crisis state. ShelterArchiveSystem may accept a historical record if its contract allows the category. PublicBroadsheetPressEngine may return a print result if the host route and input contract are made reachable. Quest ownership advances story objectives, not the world systems themselves.

Each owner call is optional and isolated. The UI reports which facts came from which owner and does not fail every source read because one optional system is unavailable. A failed archive append does not undo an already accepted print run. A missing map projection does not become an empty map. A weather query timeout does not become “clear.” If two returned facts conflict, both are surfaced with their timestamps and the player can defer a decision.

The package must avoid circular event subscriptions. A dossier reading an owner cannot cause that owner to emit a new world event; writing an archive record cannot cause the dossier to re-open; a print result cannot auto-advance a separate expedition objective unless an explicit bridge currently exists. Every command follows one direction: user action → owning command → owner result → bounded presentation update.

### Field 07 expansion — Dossier navigation, map context, and feedback

The interface uses three views: a compact timeline, a selected observation, and the owner-fact drawer. The timeline is ordered by campaign time where the source exposes it, with a visible label when only sequence order is known. The observation view shows quotation and provenance; the owner drawer shows current result and freshness. A player can compare the two without losing the selected source. The map context remains read-only and follows CartographySystem’s discovered projection.

Actions are grouped by commitment level. Read-only actions appear first. Owner-changing actions require a preview of their actual cost or consequence when the API supplies one. The final branch is separate from optional source discovery, so a player can finish the narrative without filling a completion checklist. Disabled commands explain the current owner blocker rather than suggesting another unrelated resource.

The surface must also handle no data. A newly started save with no map discoveries may show the authored place description without a blank map panel. An archive with no entries offers a first-record explanation only if the archive owner accepts it. The absence of evidence is visible and meaningful, but it is never presented as proof that no event occurred.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessibility and humane uncertainty language

The story’s uncertainty terms are part of its content schema and localization review. “Unverified” describes a source check, not a person’s honesty. “Disputed” means claims conflict, not that one witness is unreliable by default. “Stale” describes age relative to a current owner query, not the value of the historical account. These labels reduce pressure on players to make certainty judgments from tone or appearance.

The panel supports keyboard, controller, and screen-reader reading order. A player can open an observation, hear speaker/date/source, inspect current facts, return to the timeline, and decide without needing a mouse-hover tooltip. Focus indicators stay visible over map imagery. Information is not encoded only as smoke-colored overlays, fire animations, or audio alarms; text labels and symbols convey the same status. Motion can be reduced, and an alert never loops merely because the dossier remains open.

Where audio accessibility cues exist, only a real owner event may trigger them. Opening an old report cannot trigger an emergency alarm. Coalescing follows the audio coordinator’s accepted behavior, and every cue has a parallel visual notification. A player can read the complete arc with audio muted and without time-limited text.

### Field 09 expansion — Load profile and repeated-campaign economics

The dossier index is content-static and can be loaded once through the canonical catalog path; live owner projections are requested only for the selected dossier. Keep the normal screen payload bounded by pagination, and never query every region or archive item to render the first card. Story availability is evaluated from compact owner facts already exposed by the host, not by walking all survivors and all quest histories on each frame.

Performance acceptance includes an archive containing thousands of references, a map with all current regions discovered, the maximum number of dossier cards in the pack, and repeated open/close cycles while the selected survivor changes. The screen must not retain stale survivor handles or duplicate listeners. The implementation reports allocation and query-count deltas against the pre-panel route; it does not set an arbitrary target without a measured baseline.

If repeated campaigns use the same static story data, immutable catalog definitions may be shared while mutable per-campaign quest progress remains with its owner. A module load should not allocate a copy of the entire climate or map state. Any cache has a clear invalidation signal or is discarded and rebuilt on open.

### Field 10 expansion — Verification matrix and phased delivery

Phase A authors the 24 evidence-class cards and four arcs, validates references, and records unavailable consumers. Phase B presents one report through an existing quest route and proves the low-dependency ending. Phase C binds one real owner read, such as a weather access result or discovered-map projection, and proves fresh/stale/unknown behavior. Phase D adds archive or print integration only after host route and save contracts are confirmed. A landscape-fire simulation remains a separate signed package.

Focused acceptance cases include: same message received before and after a phase transition; access closure changing after the report is first viewed; undiscovered canonical location with a local name; absent archive route; repeated current query; optional audio disabled; external owner unavailable; reload after an owner result; conflicting reports; and a final unresolved path. Paired-seed verification applies only if a stateful deterministic owner is changed, not to static dialogue.

The release reviewer audits the verbs, owner references, and ending claims on every card. A card marked “confirmed” without an owner fact fails validation. A “safe route” statement without current access result fails content review. A “fire contained” ending without landscape-fire authority is rewritten as “the report was closed.” With these checks, the plan can add meaningful environmental depth without mistaking an extensive evidence narrative for an unbuilt ecology system.

## Pass 32 — Storm readiness and wildlife evidence without false causality

Current integration adds two useful environmental authorities to this expansion: `StormForecastReadinessEngine` reports forecast confidence and seasonal readiness inputs, while `WildlifeHarvestQuotaEngine` projects sustainable harvest pressure and population bands through the existing wildlife/ecology seam. These owners broaden the kind of evidence available to a landscape incident story. They do not establish that a fire occurred, that a particular storm caused it, or that a burn changed wildlife. This pass defines a campaign layer that can use their independently owned results without implying causal links the game does not calculate.

### Field 01 expansion — From warning to field account

The player receives a weather warning result, a witness account, and, later, a wildlife population or harvest projection. Each describes a different question. Forecast confidence answers how much weight to give an expected storm. Seasonal readiness describes preparation across current shelter systems. A witness describes what they saw. A wildlife projection describes an owner-calculated population/harvest condition. The incident panel presents these facts in separate lanes and lets the player compare them; it does not multiply them into a single “fire danger” or “ecosystem health” score.

The new gameplay loop is an evidence sequence: review the warning and its confidence; decide whether to ask an existing travel owner about access; collect a report or return note through a supported route; compare it with existing ecological data if available; and choose whether to annotate, circulate, or leave the dossier unresolved. Every verb has a distinct, observable outcome. A report can be closed without dispatch. A wildlife projection can be read without a harvest command. A warning can be acknowledged without changing its owner’s readiness state.

A current emergency inside the shelter takes precedence over a distant investigation. If DisasterResponseSystem reports an active shelter crisis, the player’s emergency response follows that owner. The landscape dossier can remain visible as context but cannot suppress a shelter alarm, redirect protocol activation, or automatically declare an external fire the cause of the internal event.

### Field 02 expansion — Independent evidence contracts

The warning record stores its source owner, confidence category, issue time, lead-time category, severity label, and calibration freshness only if those values are exposed by the current forecast owner. It never copies calibration decay or recomputes skill effects. The route-access record stores the result from its route/weather owner and the time that result was queried. A later change makes the old observation stale for dispatch without erasing its historical value.

The wildlife record is a read-only projection from the current wildlife owner: species or population group if available, population band, sustainable quota result if exposed, and owner timestamp. It does not claim the affected hillside is where an animal was seen unless the source also provides a canonical location. If the engine exposes a region-wide projection only, the panel labels it regional. If it exposes no fire-related variable, content cannot infer one from a decrease in population.

All three records allow “not available” as an explicit state. Missing calibration data is not a low-confidence warning. An unknown route result is not open access. A missing population record is not an extinct species. Static journal text and witness statements can remain useful while live projections are unavailable, but the UI distinguishes them from owner-confirmed facts.

### Field 03 expansion — Environmental observation data pack

The authoring pack contains separate, source-typed observations rather than a synthesized hazard catalog. Draft rows include: `OBS-STORM-ACK` (player acknowledges a warning); `OBS-WIND-RETURN` (courier returns after a delayed route); `OBS-SLOPE-REPORT` (one witness describes a dark line); `OBS-QUOTA-QUERY` (player asks to view a population projection); `OBS-HABITAT-NOTE` (field worker records a local name); and `OBS-SHELTER-ALARM` (a reported alarm that must be checked against DisasterResponseSystem). These labels are editorial placeholders, not IDs ready for production JSON.

Each row has a source class, canonical reference, stated certainty, time relevance, available owner query, possible action class, and safe closure language. Validation rejects an observation that presents an owner’s regional quota as a local animal count, a warning confidence as a probability of wildfire, or an old route note as a current dispatch permit. Content lint also flags causal conjunctions such as “because the storm passed, the herd moved” unless a live system explicitly supplies that relationship.

High-volume expansion can add many speakers and locations, but the source schema remains small. New rows should increase different points of view, communication methods, and stakes—not introduce a new derived metric for every narrative case. A catalog report groups content by actual owners and shows how many cards remain narrative-only. The report supports production review; it is not another runtime registry.

### Field 04 expansion — New story arc: The Forecast Was Right About the Wrong Thing

This five-part arc begins with a warning whose confidence is high and a later witness who reports a smoke column. A character says that the warning “proved” the smoke was a wildfire. The player checks whether the weather owner describes a severe storm; then checks whether a current location-access result exists; and, only if a supported route is available, requests a field observation. The system never treats forecast accuracy about a storm as proof of fire cause.

At the midpoint, the witness corrects the account: the visible column came from an industrial exhaust stack, but a second sound was heard beyond the mapped ridge. The first claim was partly wrong without making the witness dishonest. CartographySystem can provide a discovered-region projection if the canonical location is known. If the location is still unmapped, the player can save a quoted name and leave the location unresolved. The player’s final choice is whether to circulate a correction, preserve both accounts, or close without publication.

The ending changes the social meaning of the record, not the weather or the landscape. A correction can cite the warning and its timestamp; a preserved dispute can retain both voices; an unresolved ending says what evidence would be needed for a later report. If a print run is offered, PublicBroadsheetPressEngine supplies its own accepted cost and reach through a proven host route. No ending says a front was contained.

### Field 05 expansion — Side-quest packet: Four Ways to Read the Wild

**A Quota on the Door** asks why a hunting group wrote a number beside a shelter notice. The player can compare the note with WildlifeHarvestQuotaEngine’s present projection, ask the group for its source, or leave the number unverified. No hunting command occurs just because the player reads the quota. If the owner’s sustainable quota is zero or unavailable, the story uses the returned result rather than creating a separate moral penalty.

**Wind Without a Map** follows a scout who knows a local wind name but cannot point to a canonical map region. CartographySystem remains the location owner. The player can preserve the name as a speaker quotation or ask for an existing scouting route; neither creates a region. If a route is impossible, the side quest closes with a note that the location reference is unresolved.

**The Shelter Siren** asks whether a distant alarm is a shelter emergency or a radio recording. The player first checks the current DisasterResponseSystem state if the host exposes it. Only an active owner result opens the ordinary emergency path. Otherwise, the incident remains an information report and the player may archive the sound’s source. No second alarm manager is created.

**Numbers After Rain** has two observers who report different wildlife signs after a storm. The player retrieves both statements and compares them with an owner population projection. The projection cannot resolve which witness saw what; it only gives a separate regional fact. The reward is a more careful record and an optional follow-up dialogue, not a hidden ecology modifier.

### Field 06 expansion — Cross-system handoff map

`StormForecastReadinessEngine` can support a warning-readiness statement. `WeatherGameplayCascadeEngine` remains the owner for weather effects that it currently emits, including travel delay or location accessibility. `WildlifeHarvestQuotaEngine` owns its quota/population projection. `CartographySystem` owns discovered regions and mapped points of interest. `DisasterResponseSystem` owns acute shelter crises. `PublicBroadsheetPressEngine` owns an accepted print result. The quest owner tracks only supported narrative progression. These responsibilities cannot be collapsed into one incident event record.

An owner result may be used by a second system only through a verified host/event bridge. If the wildlife engine does not expose the location needed by the narrative route, the UI presents the projection in its proper scope and the player’s observation separately. If the forecast engine does not publish to the quest host, no quest objective is advanced from a guessed return value. The integration owner must add a narrow seam or keep the content-only path.

Failure isolation is specified per owner. An unavailable forecast leaves a witness report playable. An unavailable map projection leaves a quoted local name. A closed route offers no dispatch button. A print failure preserves the draft and does not re-run the wildlife query as compensation. One owner’s exception is never caught and misreported as a successful environmental check.

### Field 07 expansion — Observation board and safe notification states

The observation board uses explicit sections: Weather & Readiness, Route Access, Field Reports, Wildlife Projection, Shelter Emergency, and Archive/Publication. Only sections with current data are populated. Empty sections explain that no current owner result was returned; they do not display zero, green status, or blank bars. A compact view summarizes the newest fact and its source, while a detail drawer shows older statements in chronological order.

Notifications distinguish “new report,” “owner result changed,” “request refused,” and “new emergency.” A report arriving after a player closed the panel can use an existing quest/event notification if the owning route supports it. It cannot be promoted to the integrated critical audio cue for an emergency unless a real emergency owner event caused it. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator’s coalescing and visual-notification behavior is reused where available.

When a stale result changes, the player sees the old and new values with the two query times. An old high-confidence warning is not overwritten by a newer missing query. The new query may say “unable to check,” while the older warning remains a historical record. This preserves player trust and prevents uncertainty from being converted into safety.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessible cross-reference reading

Screen-reader order is section, record title, source owner, time, confidence or scope, statement, current result, then available action. In a wide map view the map is supplementary; every region label and access status appears in a linear list. High-contrast modes retain separate patterns for warning, route restriction, witness report, and unknown. A visual weather overlay never carries the only warning information.
