### Field 07 expansion — Crew agency and field workload

Vehicle rest and survivor autonomy remain separate. A survivor’s accepted help offer can be displayed beside a supported observation task, but the campaign cannot turn the offer into a seat assignment or hazard consent. A player may decline a volunteer offer, honor a refusal, or open a supported work command. Work override remains restricted to the current work owner’s legal commands and never authorizes medical intervention, privacy disclosure, or exposure to a field hazard.

The camp scene supports a low-pressure participation mode: residents can observe the map, annotate the report, or wait in the vehicle if those actions are already available to their owners. It must not invent a special “morale for camping” effect. Ideological disagreement about who receives the next field assignment uses the existing mediation system, while the actual route and deployment receipts remain unchanged.

### Field 08 expansion — Route and camp UX

The dispatch screen compares only eligible vehicles for the selected route. It presents the source of cargo, speed, defense, living capability, and bunk count. A single summary sentence provides the decision consequence: “This vehicle can deploy a camp for the current expedition; the route owner has not reported fire safety.” The player sees destination, route status, crew eligibility, requested items, camp result, and return action in that order.

Focus returns to the dispatch row after deploy or pack. The camp list is bounded to active expedition targets; historical camps are queried from their owner only when opening the journal. Repeated confirmation is blocked by the owner response, not a local campaign cooldown. Status uses text and icon plus color, and keyboard/controller back behavior returns to the prior route review without silently packing an active camp.

### Field 09 expansion — Save, replay, and performance

Vehicle module state, base-camp deployment, and vehicle rest remain in their integrated save owner. Expedition route/progress remains in ExpeditionSystem. The scenario campaign stores only references to accepted task and expedition outcomes where stable IDs exist. On restore it queries both owners and does not redeploy a camp, repeat rest, or rerun the same expedition event. If a save contains a camp ID but the current owner cannot resolve it, the journal marks the historical reference unavailable and does not fabricate a current camp.

Repeated dispatch review must be read-only. UI opens do not consume cargo, advance RNG, reorder route outcomes, change wear, or rest a survivor. Vehicle and expedition queries are grouped for the selected operation, and list filtering does not walk every item or every survivor. Performance samples include a full vehicle roster, many candidate targets, three active campaigns, and save/reload during a deployed camp if current save ownership supports that state.

### Field 10 expansion — Playable slice and acceptance gates

The first slice uses one vehicle, one canonical route, one field task, one living-module configuration, one cargo item, and one deployment/pack cycle. It proves both a valid mobile base and an otherwise identical vehicle that cannot deploy. A separate rest case exceeds bunk capacity and confirms that the vehicle owner’s result is respected. The story can complete on a survey observation without simulating or suppressing fire.

Acceptance covers route unavailable, target missing, mobile-base capability absent, capacity cap, no cargo item, item unavailable, deployment refused, camp already deployed, pack refused, save/restore with a camp, duplicate dispatch, stale environmental report, storm closure, autonomy refusal, and valid rest below/above bunk capacity. Reviewers verify that every module fact comes from VehicleCustomizationSystem, every route fact from ExpeditionSystem, and every inventory fact from the canonical inventory owner. No fire behavior, safety modifier, camp save section, vehicle condition counter, or item ledger is added by this proposal. The result adds a concrete expedition staging loop and makes field recovery logistics playable through current vehicle capabilities.
### Pass 38 supplemental field staging card bank — 24 operation seeds

These cards are a content-authoring bank for the mobile-base loop above. They are not live fire incidents or hazard modifiers. Each card may become playable only through a real route, vehicle, inventory, wildlife, weather, and recovery owner result. The narrative conclusion can be a truthful debrief even when the operation is refused.

| Candidate ID | Field setup | Owner-backed action and result |
|---|---|---|
| stage_ridge_map | A survey team is asked to revisit the ridge marker. | Query the canonical expedition target; if absent, close as “marker not mapped” without inventing a location. |
| stage_empty_bunk | The selected scout needs rest, but vehicle bunk capacity is full. | Show the vehicle owner’s cap and offer a shelter return if the expedition route accepts it. |
| stage_cargo_tarp | The team requests more gear than the projected vehicle cargo allows. | Remove optional items from the preview only; do not alter inventory until the expedition owner accepts a load. |
| stage_missing_notebook | The only requested field item is absent from canonical inventory. | Convert the visit into a no-kit observation only if the task owner accepts that reduced scope. |
| stage_no_living_module | A remote team expects to sleep beside its vehicle. | Vehicle capability refuses base-camp deployment; offer a supported nondeployment survey or return route. |
| stage_route_shift | The route status changes between preview and dispatch. | Refresh ExpeditionSystem at submit time; follow its refusal and do not create a campaign-only detour. |
| stage_wind_note | A resident reports a sudden wind shift. | Display weather-owner data if available; otherwise retain the report as an attributed observation, not a forecast. |
| stage_old_burn_mark | The team finds an old mark on a structure. | Record an authored observation; do not label it an active fire edge or infer a date without source evidence. |
| stage_animal_track | Wildlife evidence appears beside the route. | Query the wildlife owner; show species/confidence only when returned, and keep the recovery objective separate. |
| stage_camp_refused | The expedition permits arrival but the vehicle refuses camp deployment. | Keep the accepted visit distinct from the failed camp action and return through the current route owner. |
| stage_pack_after_visit | A complete observation is ready for return. | Call the existing camp-pack action, then close only after its receipt; do not delete an active camp locally. |
| stage_vehicle_swap | The first selected vehicle cannot meet route/cargo requirements. | Re-run the existing vehicle and expedition projections for another canonical vehicle, without cloning its module state. |
| stage_crew_declines | A survivor refuses the optional field assignment. | Honor the autonomy/work response and let the dispatch owner choose an eligible replacement only if supported. |
| stage_volunteer_offer | A survivor offers to annotate the route record. | Show the autonomy event; accept only through a valid owner command and keep annotation separate from hazard exposure. |
| stage_mediation_pause | Two residents disagree about who should publish the report. | Offer existing mediation choices; the resulting social receipt cannot change route safety or field observations. |
| stage_return_window | Weather closes a current route after the visit. | Ask the expedition owner for accepted return options and show “return route unavailable” if none exists. |
| stage_broken_label | A location label conflicts with the canonical map record. | Preserve the source ID, show a map-review task, and prevent narrative text from rewriting the canonical label. |
| stage_survey_only | The destination is reachable but no environmental measurement owner accepts a test. | Complete a visual report and explicitly mark measured hazard as unavailable. |
| stage_filter_unmade | A research breakthrough is known, but its item is absent. | Show unlock and inventory as separate states; offer an existing crafting route only if it resolves. |
| stage_scrubber_unbuilt | Shelter ventilation research is unlocked but the upgrade is not installed. | Report the actual installation owner state and do not declare a field camp filtered. |
| stage_false_shelter_claim | A character calls an armored vehicle “fireproof.” | Present the exact module result and correct the claim without applying hidden damage or protection. |
| stage_target_archived | A prior campaign report references a target no longer available. | Render the stable historical receipt if the journal owns one; never spawn a duplicate map target. |
| stage_long_roster | Many survivors could be eligible for a visit. | Filter by existing assignment/eligibility queries and resolve details only for the chosen crew. |
| stage_duplicate_dispatch | The player double-submits a deployment after a delayed response. | Use the vehicle/expedition owner’s accepted state and idempotent command response; do not add local camp debouncing state. |

## Pass 38 supplemental prose and reward rules

Rewards for this route are narrative and evidentiary unless an existing owner returns a gameplay result. A field note can unlock a later dialogue scene through the current quest or journal owner; it cannot award generic “fire knowledge,” a protection buff, or a new collectible ledger. Any item reward must be granted by canonical inventory. A survivor who returns tired is not automatically injured; needs or health owners must report that fact.

The visit may close with one of three authored statements: “The team made the supported survey and returned”; “the team reached the site but could not deploy its requested camp”; or “the route owner declined the visit.” A neutral acknowledgment is offered for any absent measurement. These endings keep the play loop complete without disguising unsupported fire mechanics as outcomes.
## Pass 38 worked sequence — The ridge survey that had to turn back

The worked sequence demonstrates a complete recovery visit through current vehicle and expedition owners while keeping the fire-model gap visible.

1. The recovery board opens a previously authored field request. It shows the request source, a canonical target ID, and its age. If the target ID no longer resolves, the sequence ends as a mapping task and does not create a replacement target.
2. The player opens the route review. ExpeditionSystem returns one current path and one unavailable candidate. Only the returned path is shown as dispatchable; the unavailable line has no guessed travel duration.
3. The player selects a vehicle. The system displays its aggregated speed, cargo, defense, module categories, and whether it can serve as a mobile base. Defense is labeled as the owner’s current projection and is never translated into heat or smoke protection.
4. The requested survey kit is checked against the canonical inventory and vehicle cargo projection. A missing notebook changes the planned deliverable to a visual observation only if the task owner supports that reduced scope.
5. Research readiness shows a completed air-filtration unlock. Inventory reports that the named item is absent, and the shelter owner reports no installed upgrade. The player sees three independent statuses and cannot conclude that the outdoor team has filtered air.
6. One survivor offers to annotate a route. SurvivorAutonomySystem emits its owner event. The player accepts the supported annotation action; no work override or hazard-consent shortcut is available.
7. A second survivor declines the visit. The roster/work owner removes that person from the proposed crew only if its existing command allows it. The player chooses a different eligible crew member; the refusal is not recorded as a negative character trait.
8. The vehicle owner accepts the base-camp deployment. The UI reports deployment and lists the returned vehicle configuration. It does not call the site a shelter or refuge.
9. The player initiates the actual survey through the accepted expedition task. The narrative describes observations and witnesses. It cannot apply fire damage or claim suppression.
10. The wildlife owner returns a migration observation. It is stored or linked through its existing journal path. The campaign reports it beside, not as a cause of, the landscape scars.
11. The weather owner later returns a route warning. The expedition owner determines whether the team can complete the remaining observation or must return.
12. If the route is refused, the player follows the owner-returned route action. A story line does not force a safe passage or award a route token.
13. The player packs the camp using VehicleCustomizationSystem. A refusal is displayed as a live camp-state issue; the campaign cannot erase the deployment record to close the quest.
14. On arrival, only accepted owner receipts appear in the report: route, camp, survey, wildlife observation, and return. No inferred burn edge or exposure reading is added.
15. A final conversation asks whether the report should be shared. Existing publication consent and journal owners determine the action. The result closes the episode and leaves any unsupported fire behavior explicitly unavailable.

The failure path is equally complete: an unmapped site yields a map-review task; a vehicle without living capacity yields a nondeployment visit; a missing item narrows the survey; a refused route returns to planning; an unaccepted environmental query is reported as unknown; and a pack refusal remains visible. None of those outcomes creates a second vehicle, route, inventory, fire, or save authority.
## Pass 39 — Warning mesh, mapped evidence, and disaster-response recovery

This pass adds an incident-intelligence layer to burn recovery by composing current CommunicationsSystem, DisasterResponseSystem, CartographySystem, WeatherGameplayCascadeSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, and AudioAccessibilityCoordinator results. It does not create a wildfire spread simulation, a second radio network, a second map, a new disaster ledger, or a hidden smoke model. The player receives a clearer chain from warning to route choice to response protocol to archival report. Every claim remains owner-stamped.

### Field 01 expansion — Incident eligibility from the disaster owner

The recovery board can display an acute disaster only when DisasterResponseSystem returns an active crisis, a supported archetype, or a resolved response receipt. Its existing archetypes include electrical fire, flooding, radiation breach, air-toxin leak, earthquake, and structural subsidence. “Wildland fire” remains a content label unless the current disaster catalog and host route identify a corresponding owner state. A narrative burn mark cannot open an emergency protocol by itself.

The board distinguishes ACTIVE, CONTAINED, RESOLVED, and NO_OWNER_RESULT. A contained shelter electrical fire can motivate a field inspection story, but it is not evidence that a nearby landscape is burning. A resolved disaster may supply a historical entry, while a current expedition requires a separate route and target. The player can still accept an authored observation task when the disaster owner has no matching outdoor event, but the task is explicitly observational.

### Field 02 expansion — Warning channels and reception

CommunicationsSystem is the sole authority for antenna tier, reception range, interception, decoding, broadcast reach, jamming, and condition. Recovery content can request a broadcast, decode an incoming warning, or inspect a signal result. It cannot assign a radio range, mark a location safe because a message arrived, or make an unverified transmission authoritative.

The warning card records frequency/network, signal state, source identity if returned, decoded/undecoded state, and age. An intercepted message is evidence with provenance; a decoded message is not automatically a map update or disaster trigger. A jammed signal explains why the recovery team lacks a current warning. The player may choose a local survey or return route only through existing expedition commands.

### Field 03 expansion — Cartographic target and confidence

CartographySystem supplies map regions, discovery, surveys, point-of-interest mapping, equipment bonuses, cartographer proficiency, map acquisition, completeness, and a read-only world projection. A recovery operation binds to a canonical region or POI. If the map only knows a region, the story cannot invent a precise burn perimeter. If a survey returns a POI, the report cites that POI and its owner timestamp.

The plan adds three content-facing labels: REGION_KNOWN, POINT_MAPPED, and FIELD_OBSERVATION_PENDING. They are projections, not a new map state. A compass or cartography kit contributes only through the cartography owner. A narrative sketch can be attached to an archive entry, but it cannot silently call DiscoverRegion or advance map completeness.

### Field 04 expansion — Protocol choice at a real crisis

When DisasterResponseSystem returns an active supported crisis, the recovery board can show existing response protocols and their current owner results. The owner’s documented mitigation bounds—up to 70 percent damage reduction, labor synergy up to 75 percent, and resilience-based response speed—remain with that system. A player choice such as “send a repair crew” calls the response owner; it does not calculate a burn-fighting bonus in this plan.

The content separates crisis containment from expedition recovery. A contained electrical fire may release a shelter corridor for a later inspection. It does not open an outdoor route, clear weather closure, or reduce a landscape hazard. If the owner has no protocol for the requested story, the UI presents a read-only recommendation and a foreman gap rather than a fake action.

### Field 05 expansion — Weather cascade and route timing

WeatherGameplayCascadeSystem remains the source for location closures, expedition delay forecasts, shelter thermal/filtration stress, market shocks, and mental-health stress where its current templates apply. The recovery plan reads the returned delay/closure and cites it beside radio and cartography evidence. It does not run another forecast, reroll the daily weather, or convert a delay into fire spread.

An incident card can show “route closed by weather cascade,” “route delayed,” or “no current weather effect reported.” The return path is determined by ExpeditionSystem. The same weather result is not applied twice because the recovery panel only projects the owner’s receipt. An authored line may describe wind, ash, or cold as observed atmosphere, but it cannot add a numeric exposure consequence without an owner.

### Field 06 expansion — Audio and visual warning equivalence

AudioAccessibilityCoordinator already maps critical cues for alarms, low power, geiger escalation, incoming raids, medical emergency, expedition return, and radio signal. The recovery package binds each supported incident notification to one of these existing cues or to a plain text journal update. It does not add an outdoor-fire cue unless the audio owner approves a new catalog row and consumer.

Visual notifications, coalescing windows, ducking, and reduced-stimulation mix presets remain owner behavior. A radio signal may produce a concise visual notification even when sound is muted. Multiple reports from one coalescing window become one readable notice with source count and latest timestamp. The recovery board never depends on hearing a siren to reveal a critical route blocker.

### Field 07 expansion — Storyline: The Siren Map

Chapter one opens with a radio signal that CommunicationsSystem can receive but not decode. The shelter archive contains an older map fragment for the same region. The player chooses whether to send a cartographer, wait for a better antenna condition, or follow an already-supported route. No option claims to know the fire perimeter.

Chapter two decodes a message naming a mapped industrial region and a closed road. WeatherCascadeSystem confirms the route closure. DisasterResponseSystem reports a resolved electrical fire at the shelter, which explains why the warning network is stressed but does not prove the external event. The player publishes a carefully scoped warning and asks CartographySystem to update a POI after a valid survey.

Chapter three returns a field observation: burned fencing, intact concrete, and a displaced animal track. The archive records the observation and source. The final scene is about institutional memory: the settlement keeps the siren, the map, and the uncertainty together. The player earns trust for accurate reporting, not for claiming to have solved an unmodeled fire.

### Field 08 expansion — Side-quest bank routing

The side quests in the supplemental bank use one owner action each: decode a warning, map a target, inspect a resolved shelter disaster, relay a broadcast, compare a route delay, verify a response protocol, or archive a report. A quest may chain these actions, but it stores stable references instead of copying their state. Failure still produces a readable ending: signal jammed, map incomplete, route closed, protocol unavailable, survey inconclusive, or report archived.

No quest awards an outdoor suppression buff, a smoke-resistance item, or an ecological recovery score. Any ordinary item, reputation change, or morale result must be returned by an existing owner. The narrative layer can reward careful uncertainty with an archive milestone only when ShelterArchiveSystem accepts the entry.

### Field 09 expansion — Save, determinism, and evidence custody

Communications, disaster, cartography, weather, archive, and audio systems retain their own save sections and deterministic streams. Recovery episode state stores only stable owner references, accepted quest identifiers, and the text/source metadata allowed by the campaign journal. Reload must not re-decode a message, rediscover a region, re-trigger a disaster, or emit a second archive entry.

The evidence view is immutable for a completed report. If a live owner changes after the report, the journal labels the historical receipt and displays current state separately. If an older save lacks a source reference, the report degrades to “historical detail unavailable” instead of guessing. Same-seed runs with the same owner state produce identical route, protocol, and record choices.

### Field 10 expansion — Promotion gates and load profile

The slice promotes only after one radio signal, one mapped region, one weather route result, one supported disaster protocol, one audio/visual notification, and one archive receipt are reachable through existing hosts. A second slice covers a signal jam, unmapped POI, route closure, unsupported protocol, muted audio, and reload.

Performance review measures one open warning panel, many stored archive entries, eight regions, several active messages, multiple coalesced cues, and a long recovery quest list. The panel uses compact projections and lazy detail reads. Acceptance proves that no event is doubled, no source is made authoritative by prose, and no unsupported outdoor-fire mechanic is smuggled into a disaster or weather owner.

### Pass 39 supplemental incident-evidence bank — 24 records

| Candidate ID | Evidence combination | Bounded player result |
|---|---|---|
| warning_unread | Radio message received but not decoded | Keep as unread evidence; offer decoder route only if CommunicationsSystem supports it. |
| warning_jammed | Current network is jammed | Show stale/absent warning and an accepted local survey option if one exists. |
| region_known_only | Cartography knows a region but no POI | Send a canonical regional survey; do not draw a perimeter. |
| poi_mapped | A POI is mapped with owner receipt | Attach the observation to that POI and preserve its source. |
| electrical_fire_resolved | Shelter disaster owner reports resolved | Open a shelter follow-up, never an outdoor fire event. |
| air_toxin_active | Disaster owner reports an active air-toxin leak | Use its protocol and medical/air owner outcomes; do not call it smoke. |
| weather_closed | Cascade closes a location | Block the route through ExpeditionSystem and show a return option. |
| weather_delayed | Cascade forecasts delay | Let the expedition owner apply its delay; no second travel penalty. |
| radio_broadcast | Broadcast command is accepted | Record transmission receipt; recipients are not invented. |
| source_unverified | Message source is missing | Mark origin unknown and avoid faction attribution. |
| map_purchase | Commercial map acquisition is available | Call CartographySystem; do not increase knowledge twice. |
| survey_compass | Compass survey is accepted | Apply only the cartography owner’s equipment bonus. |
| survey_kit | Cartography kit is available | Show the owner’s larger bonus if returned; no custom bonus. |
| protocol_available | Disaster protocol can be activated | Display actual owner mitigation result. |
| protocol_missing | Requested protocol has no current owner | Close as a design gap or observation, not as a failed hidden action. |
| shelter_alarm | Existing alarm cue fires | Use the integrated visual notification and coalescing behavior. |
| radio_cue_muted | Player uses reduced stimulation | Keep text and icon visible while respecting mix preset. |
| report_conflict | Two reports disagree | Preserve both sources and ask for a supported verification task. |
| archive_duplicate | Same receipt is submitted twice | ShelterArchiveSystem or campaign owner returns exact-once behavior. |
| old_map | Archived map is older than current region state | Show historical and current projections separately. |
| route_return | A team must return from a closed route | Call the current expedition return action. |
| animal_observation | Wildlife owner returns track data | Archive it as adjacent evidence, not fire causality. |
| survivor_refuses | Assigned observer refuses work | Honor autonomy/work owner result and seek an eligible alternative. |
| no_measurement | No environmental measurement owner responds | Complete an observation report with unknown measurement state. |

### Pass 39 supplemental acceptance narrative

The player should be able to finish the episode after any one of the following: successful warning relay, careful map update, supported disaster containment, safe route return, or honest archival report. “Solved the fire” is reserved for a future owner-backed mechanic. This keeps the expansion playable now while leaving a precise seam for a later outdoor hazard system.
## Pass 40 — Recovery crews, forward camps, and practical knowledge transfer

This pass turns a successful warning/observation route into a longer recovery service by composing colony/outpost infrastructure, survivor education, hobby practice, communications, and archive evidence. It focuses on what people can learn and maintain after an incident without adding a new skill tree or a “firefighter” profession. Colony and outpost owners decide whether a location exists and can be supplied; SurvivorEducationSystem owns curricula and knowledge; HobbySystem owns leisure mastery; CommunicationsSystem owns the relay; Archive owns the institutional record.

### Field 01 expansion — Forward location as a work context

Recovery content can reference a canonical colony or outpost as a staging context. ColonySystem and OutpostSettlementSystem return capacity, supply, garrison, condition, building, and risk. The plan does not treat a named camp as a newly created settlement. A forward site can host a meeting or record review even when it cannot support a field expedition.

The card distinguishes destination exists, route accepted, supplies available, and recovery action accepted. A watchtower or depot is infrastructure; it is not a fire lookout or a medical station unless its owner provides that capability. An overrun or starving site can still contribute a historical archive reference without being presented as currently operational.

### Field 02 expansion — Education subjects for recovery literacy

SurvivorEducationSystem owns age stage, teacher/student assignments, prerequisites, study ticks, skill unlocks, graduation, and shelter knowledge. The recovery campaign may author lessons that use existing curriculum subjects such as medicine, engineering, survival, agriculture, communications, or history only when the catalog returns them. A lesson can teach how to read a warning or archive an observation; it cannot grant an unregistered firefighting skill.

Teaching results are owner receipts. A parent-child bonus or schoolroom bonus comes only from the education owner. The campaign may offer an adult refresher or apprentice lesson as a side quest, but it cannot advance knowledge by dialogue choice. A learner can fail, pause, or graduate, and each outcome has its own prose.

### Field 03 expansion — Hobbies as recovery practice

HobbySystem owns ten hobbies across Creative, Intellectual, Physical, Social, Crafting, and Collecting categories, facility gates, group sessions, mastery tiers, affinity, and persistence. Recovery content can use drawing, map-making, radio tinkering, repair craft, or collecting as character texture and optional practice. A hobby session is not work assignment, field hazard training, or an incident response protocol.

A survivor who reaches an owner-reported mastery tier may unlock an authored conversation or archive prompt. The prompt cannot change cartography, communications, or disaster state unless the current owner accepts a real action. Group hobby morale remains the hobby owner’s result, separate from recovery reputation.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Map Room After the Smoke

After the Siren Map episode, the player finds that three residents remember the route differently. One has cartography training, one completed a communications lesson, and one keeps a collection of old emergency labels. Education and Hobby owners report their current states. The player invites them to a map-room session through supported leisure/education routes.

The group produces a reviewed observation packet: a corrected location label, a radio-frequency note, and an archive citation. CartographySystem accepts a POI correction only through its command, CommunicationsSystem accepts a test transmission only through its command, and ShelterArchiveSystem records a milestone only after the owner accepts. A resident who refuses the session is not pressured. The story resolves through careful collaboration, not a bonus invented by the recovery plan.

### Field 05 expansion — Maintenance literacy and handoff

The plan authors short tasks for checking filters, inspecting a relay, reading a route board, cataloging supplies, and preserving a map. Each task declares its owner. If no maintenance command exists, the player can only record a request or observation. The project never decrements condition or consumes material on its own.

A completed lesson can change who is eligible for a future owner command if SurvivorEducationSystem returns the relevant skill unlock. It cannot assign the survivor automatically. Duty roster, work owner, and autonomy owner decide whether the person accepts the task. The handoff card names what was learned, what was attempted, and what remains unowned.

### Field 06 expansion — Seasonal and climate pressure

NuclearWinterProgressionSystem supplies phase, season, temperature, daylight, heating demand, expedition hazard surge, greenhouse preservation, jitter, and anomaly results. Recovery prose can schedule a lesson or archive review during deep winter, pale spring, ash summer, or black autumn. It may use the returned conditions to explain timing, but it does not add a new fire season or weather penalty.

SeasonalCelebrationSystem may provide a holiday or anniversary around which a memorial map review occurs. The system owns costs and streaks. Skipping a celebration is not a recovery failure unless the celebration owner returns that consequence. A climate anomaly can close a route through WeatherCascadeSystem, leaving the lesson safe and the expedition deferred.

### Field 07 expansion — Communications practice without signal invention

An education or hobby scene may rehearse decoding, antenna care, or message etiquette. A real transmission, reception, decoding, or jam result still requires CommunicationsSystem. The scene cannot “practice” by consuming a signal, changing antenna range, or creating a message recipient. A fictional exercise is labeled as such.

The UI distinguishes training simulation, test transmission, received field message, and acknowledged warning. If the signal is not delivered, the story can end with a learner understanding why. This supports compelling character growth without turning authored prose into network state.

### Field 08 expansion — Archive as institutional curriculum

ShelterArchiveSystem can supply old decisions, events, memorials, milestones, discoveries, and achievements for a lesson. A learner searches a filtered projection, reads allowed text, and may submit a new entry through an accepted owner path. Archive search is read-only; it does not unlock a reward by itself.

Private memorial details remain protected. A public recovery lesson uses redacted or attributed facts. The archive stores the final accepted report, not every draft. The curriculum can teach source criticism by presenting contradictory reports, with the resolution outcome determined by Cartography, Communications, or quest owners rather than by the lesson script.

### Field 09 expansion — Persistence and replay

Education, hobby, colony, outpost, communications, weather, celebration, archive, and recovery quest state retain their own save ownership. The expansion stores references to accepted lessons, sessions, messages, and reports. Reload does not repeat study, advance mastery, spend celebration resources, send a message, or archive the same milestone.

Same-seed runs with equal learner, facility, day, and owner state produce equal study/mastery outcomes. Opening the recovery curriculum is read-only and does not tick a day. A large archive and many learners use filtered queries; the panel does not scan every survivor on every frame.

### Field 10 expansion — Long-term promotion

Promotion requires one canonical forward site, one accepted lesson, one hobby session, one message test, one map/archive receipt, and one weather/season projection. It must also prove a refusal path, an unowned maintenance request, a winter route delay, and reload. No new fire skill, season, camp condition, or reputation authority is added.

The result is a sustainable aftermath loop: survivors learn how to preserve evidence, maintain current equipment where owners support it, communicate honestly, and remember what happened. It makes recovery deeper without pretending that a lesson is a hazard simulation.

The preferred endings are “the learners can read the record,” “the test signal was not received,” “the map correction remains pending,” “the forward site is historical,” and “the class was postponed.” These are playable outcomes with human meaning and no unsupported mechanical reward.
## Pass 41 — Recovery command center, incident queues, and high-volume field records

This pass specifies a high-volume command-center view for recovery work. It is a read model over existing disaster, weather, expedition, cartography, communications, survivor, vehicle, archive, and accessibility owners. It is not a new incident scheduler or danger meter. The goal is to make dozens of reports, route requests, and return receipts usable without losing provenance or causing duplicate work.

### Field 01 expansion — Queue entries have an owner and a reason

Each queue row has a stable row ID, owner kind, source ID, current status, last update day, supported action IDs, and a one-sentence reason. The recovery plan never sorts rows by an invented danger score. If a disaster owner returns ACTIVE, the row may be high priority; if WeatherCascadeSystem returns a route closure, the row may be blocked; if Cartography returns an unmapped region, the row may be informational. The owner’s state is the fact.

Rows can be grouped by incident, route, shelter, colony, or archive record. Grouping is a presentation projection and has no mutable group state. A group expands into its owner receipts on demand. A missing owner response is visible as unknown, not zero urgency.

### Field 02 expansion — Priority without hidden gameplay

The panel supports filters such as active owner event, player-requested follow-up, route blocker, evidence awaiting review, archived, and stale. A player can pin a row, but a pin does not change simulation priority. The current disaster or expedition owner decides what is urgent in the world.

If two rows compete for one crew, the work/roster owner receives the assignment command. The panel explains that the crew is unavailable and does not decide by comparing prose adjectives. A player can defer an information row without changing its source.

### Field 03 expansion — Daily refresh and event-driven updates

When an owner emits a current seam, the command center refreshes the affected row only. If no seam exists, an explicit refresh queries selected owner projections. It never polls every disaster, every message, and every archive entry every frame. The daily campaign tick remains the source of time.

Updates carry sequence or timestamp when the owner provides one. An older receipt cannot overwrite a newer one. If the owner has no ordering field, the panel displays last-query order and avoids claiming chronology. Duplicate notifications are coalesced by AudioAccessibilityCoordinator where applicable.

### Field 04 expansion — Incident bundle expansion

A row may expand into weather, radio, map, disaster, route, crew, and archive subfacts. Each subfact shows source, state, and supported action. The bundle does not calculate a composite outcome. “Route closed” can coexist with “message decoded” and “shelter disaster resolved.”

An incident bundle can be saved as a player view preference only through UI settings if that owner exists. It cannot be persisted as a new gameplay entity. Closing and reopening the bundle reads current owner state and distinguishes historical receipt from live status.

### Field 05 expansion — Crew and vehicle availability

The command center may query current survivor eligibility, autonomy/refusal events, vehicle capability, cargo, bunk capacity, and expedition route. It does not cache a private crew roster as authority. A refusal is shown as a refusal; a vehicle without a living module is shown as nondeployable; a full bunk is shown as a capacity boundary.

Selecting a replacement crew member invokes the existing roster/work/expedition route. The panel cannot turn a help offer into an assignment or a rest result into a medical result. Long rosters use a bounded list and resolve details after selection.

### Field 06 expansion — Data volume and content generation

The first high-volume pack provides 36 incident records across message, weather, map, disaster, wildlife observation, route, crew, camp, and archive types. Each record includes a source requirement, a no-source fallback, a supported action, a non-actionable observation, and a closure sentence. Authors can vary names, voices, and settlement context without altering mechanics.

Records are data-driven, snake_case IDs, and owner references only. They do not introduce a second incident JSON authority or require runtime code to interpret arbitrary script expressions. A validator rejects unknown owner kinds and unsupported action names before the records enter a playable catalog.

### Field 07 expansion — Accessibility in a dense board

The board exposes a summary count, current filter, focused row, owner source, blocker, and next action as text. Icons pair with words. Audio notifications remain optional, and reduced-stimulation mode uses the existing preset. Screen readers receive the same source and consequence order as visual users.

Focus moves from filter to row list to detail to action and returns to the prior row after completion. A player can dismiss a row without deleting its owner event. A long report is paged and has a direct return action. No critical blocker appears only in a tooltip.

### Field 08 expansion — Failure and stale-state language

Approved states include current, historical, stale, unknown, pending owner, rejected, and unavailable. “Stale” means the owner returned a fact outside the panel’s freshness rule; it does not mean false. “Historical” means the archive owns the record; it does not mean current. “Pending” means an accepted action has not returned a final result.

If a route closes after the player opens the panel, submit rechecks the owner. A failed action leaves the row and reason visible. A successful action does not remove the historical receipt. A save migration that loses a stable ID produces an explicit unavailable row.

### Field 09 expansion — Persistence, migration, and determinism

The command center persists only view settings and stable references if the existing UI/settings owner allows it. All live state remains in current systems. A migration never serializes a snapshot of every owner into recovery state. Same seed and same owner saves yield equal row ordering where ordering is owner-defined.

Opening, sorting, filtering, and expanding rows are side-effect-free. Save/reload after a dispatch, message, map discovery, archive record, or camp return does not replay the action. Older saves lacking new optional fields receive neutral display defaults.

### Field 10 expansion — Performance gate and vertical slice

The performance slice contains 100 archive entries, 24 active/closed messages, eight map regions, six disaster records, ten candidate routes, two vehicles, twelve survivors, and thirty-six authored incident rows. It measures initial open, filter change, row expansion, action submit, close/reopen, save/reload, and notification coalescing.

Promotion requires bounded reads, listener disposal, exact-once actions, source labels, accessible fallback, and no extra state owner. The command center is ready when it can be busy without becoming misleading.

### Pass 41 supplemental worked run

The player opens the board with 100 rows. The filter narrows to route blockers. A weather closure, a jammed radio, and an unmapped POI remain. The player selects the radio row and sends a supported decoder action; the weather row remains unaffected. A cartography survey maps the POI, but expedition still refuses travel. The player archives the evidence, receives a visual notification rather than a repeated alarm, saves, reloads, and sees the same historical report plus current route refusal. The entire loop produces no new fire model, no duplicate action, and no false certainty.
## Pass 42 — Recovery performance, lifecycle, and regression scaffolding

This pass specifies how a large recovery expansion stays fast and honest as content volume grows. It covers panel lifecycle, owner subscriptions, query grouping, archival pagination, deterministic replay, accessibility snapshots, and negative-case regression. It does not change the simulation owners.

### Field 01 expansion — Composition-root binding

The recovery surface receives existing host services through the composition root. It does not construct a second WeatherCascadeSystem, CommunicationsSystem, CartographySystem, or DisasterResponseSystem for a preview. A missing service produces a disabled/read-only route with a diagnostic. Binding occurs once per session and is released on teardown.

### Field 02 expansion — Projection boundaries

Each owner exposes a compact projection for the selected incident. The panel composes projections by stable IDs and source labels. It does not serialize full owner objects into a view model. A projection can be absent, stale, or unsupported and remains visibly so.

### Field 03 expansion — Listener lifecycle

Listeners for radio, disaster, weather, expedition return, audio notification, archive, and autonomy seams are attached on open and detached on close. Reopen stability is measured over 100 cycles. A closed panel cannot emit a duplicate warning or retain a survivor reference.

### Field 04 expansion — Query and cache policy

Metadata lists are cached only for the panel lifetime. Current owner state is refreshed after an owner event, submit, explicit refresh, or reload. No per-frame query scans all regions, messages, archive entries, or survivors. A cache key includes owner/source ID and session identity.

### Field 05 expansion — Deterministic replay

The replay harness opens the same incident sequence twice with the same seed, owner saves, and input choices. It compares decoded message results, weather route state, cartography receipt, disaster protocol outcome, archive IDs, and notification count. A UI-only open must not advance any value.

### Field 06 expansion — Save envelope boundaries

Recovery state uses existing campaign/quest references and owner save sections. Migration tests cover absent optional references, renamed display text, historical records without source IDs, and an active route restored after a weather closure. The panel never repairs a malformed owner envelope.

### Field 07 expansion — Accessibility regression

Snapshot cases cover warning text, muted audio, reduced-stimulation preset, high contrast, keyboard/controller focus, screen-reader source labels, long archive page, blocked route, and action confirmation. The accessibility owner’s visual notifications are compared against the audio cue result.

### Field 08 expansion — Failure observability

Every blocked action returns a stable reason code or an explicit unavailable state. Logs identify owner and action without secrets or private patient data. Unknown owner errors are surfaced to the review report and do not become generic success.

### Field 09 expansion — Memory and long-session profile

The profile runs a recovery campaign for many in-game days with repeated open/close, archive search, radio updates, and route changes. It checks listener counts, retained strings, projection cache size, and notification queue growth. A completed historical report is compact and immutable.

### Field 10 expansion — Gate package

The gate package includes lifecycle, replay, migration, accessibility, performance, source-trace, and negative-owner fixtures. A clean compile is insufficient; a route is promoted only when the observable output matches its owner. No broad test suite is mandated by this document; the integrator selects focused targets.

## Pass 43 — High-volume recovery narrative deck and owner-state matrix

This pass supplies a large authoring deck for repeated recovery visits. The cards use the command-center, warning, map, disaster, route, vehicle, survivor, archive, and education boundaries already defined. Each card has a playable human situation, an owner-backed action, and a truthful closure.

### Field 01 expansion — Report cards

Every card contains a title, location reference, source owner, first observable fact, player decision, possible owner result, fallback, public/private label, and archive policy. Writers may vary voice and weather texture while preserving this structure. A card without a canonical source remains a draft.

### Field 02 expansion — Encounter density

The deck supports one-time, repeatable, seasonal, and follow-up visits. Repeatability is controlled by the existing quest/archive owner, not by a local cooldown. A repeat visit can reveal a new owner result without rewriting the old report.

### Field 03 expansion — Evidence prose

Field prose separates what a character sees, hears, remembers, and measures. “Ash on the rail” is observation. “The fire crossed the valley” is a causal claim requiring an owner. “The radio says the road is closed” is a communications receipt whose route effect requires Expedition/Weather owners.

### Field 04 expansion — Decision variety

Cards offer wait, verify, communicate, reroute, archive, help, decline, and return choices. They do not force combat or firefighting. A player can complete a card by choosing careful uncertainty.

### Field 05 expansion — Survivor voices

Voices vary by education, hobby, relationship, grief, duty, and experience only when the respective owner returns those facts. Text never diagnoses a survivor or predicts their action from a trait that is not available.

### Field 06 expansion — Failure texture

Failure prose names the blocker and leaves a next step: the signal is jammed, the map is incomplete, the route is closed, the owner is unavailable, the crew declines, or the archive cannot accept the record. A failure does not erase effort.

### Field 07 expansion — Reward and consequence

Rewards are owner-backed items, archive milestones, accepted messages, map receipts, route outcomes, or character scenes. Consequences are owner-backed delay, refusal, closure, or unresolved evidence. There is no generic “fire preparedness” score.

### Field 08 expansion — UI copy matrix

Each card supplies short status text, long explanation, action label, disabled reason, success line, failure line, and accessibility description. Text is source-aware and localization-ready.

### Field 09 expansion — Batch production

Authors can release the deck in batches of twelve records. Each batch must include a source audit, one negative case, one accessibility case, one reload case, and one archive/privacy review. A high-volume batch is not approved by prose volume alone.

### Field 10 expansion — Deck acceptance

The initial deck contains 48 records below. Promotion requires owner routes for the selected pilot subset and preview-only treatment for the remainder. This permits a large story library without falsely making every card playable.

### Pass 43 supplemental prose protocol

Every card ends with a sentence that tells the player what is known, what is not known, and where to look next. For example: “The fence is burned and the route is closed; no owner has measured a moving fire. The map desk can keep the report, or the expedition can wait.” This format makes uncertainty a playable result rather than a blank screen.
## Pass 44 — Cross-plan recovery handoff and implementation order

This pass gives the four-plan wave an explicit handoff order. Plan 1 owns recovery content and references the other plans only through their existing owner seams.

### Field 01 expansion — Shared location identity

Plan 1 accepts canonical location/region IDs from Cartography and expedition owners. Plans 2–4 may reference the same location only through stable IDs and owner projections.

### Field 02 expansion — Shared incident evidence

Radio, weather, disaster, wildlife, and archive receipts are shared facts. No plan republishes them as mutable state.

### Field 03 expansion — Shared survivor agency

Autonomy, refusal, help, education, hobby, and work events remain survivor-owned. Recovery consumes receipts and honors consent.

### Field 04 expansion — Shared vehicle/route

Vehicle and expedition owners determine cargo, camp, rest, route, and return. Recovery content supplies objectives only.

### Field 05 expansion — Shared public memory

Archive and memorial owners decide what becomes institutional history. A recovery report can be proposed or archived, never silently both.

### Field 06 expansion — Shared accessibility

AudioAccessibilityCoordinator owns critical cue presentation. All four plans provide text and focus fallbacks.

### Field 07 expansion — Shared data review

New recovery rows require schema, ID, source, consumer, save, and failure evidence. A plan row alone is not approval.

### Field 08 expansion — Shared performance

Each plan uses metadata-first lists, selected-detail queries, bounded subscriptions, and no per-frame world scans.

### Field 09 expansion — Shared save boundary

Recovery references owner saves and current campaign/quest state. It does not add a cross-plan save section.

### Field 10 expansion — Handoff order

Verify owners, prototype one route, add content batch, run focused checks, review accessibility, then consider broader scale.

## Pass 45 — Burn-scar stewardship, evidence quality, and long-tail recovery

This pass extends recovery beyond the first safe return. The burn scar is treated as a changing field of evidence, labor, memory, and future risk. It does not introduce a fire ledger, a new hazard authority, or a parallel ecology simulation. It asks existing weather, location, expedition, inventory, archive, colony, and disaster owners for facts and turns those facts into bounded work.

### Field 01 expansion — Scar classification

A location can be tagged with a descriptive scar class such as ash_strip, heat_shocked, smoke_stained, waterline_burn, collapsed_edge, or recovered_green. The tag is an observed projection with a source and observation time. It is not a new damage counter. A later survey can replace the class when the owning location or disaster system reports a different state. The UI shows “last observed” and “source,” so an old photograph cannot masquerade as a current route verdict.

### Field 02 expansion — Residual hazard questions

Recovery cards ask explicit questions: is the surface stable, is the air acceptable, is water clear, is the route open, and is the structure occupied? Each answer is supplied by an existing owner or marked unknown. Unknown is a valid state that blocks a risky action and creates a measurement task. This prevents the plan from inferring safety from the mere absence of a new alert.

### Field 03 expansion — Soil and garden handoff

A burn-scar garden scene references Agriculture, greenhouse, cooking, and inventory owners. It may request seed, clean water, ash-safe containers, or labor, but it does not calculate fertility. A successful scene records a garden project receipt and lets the agriculture owner decide whether a crop can actually be planted. A failed scene can produce a lesson, a memorial, or a delayed route without silently changing yield.

### Field 04 expansion — Salvage triage

Salvage is presented as a triage queue with labels intact, contaminated, warped, missing, or unverified. Inventory owns item identity and condition. Recovery owns the question, the evidence photograph, and the next action. A card that says “three sealed tins found” must receive an inventory receipt before the player can spend them. If the receipt fails, the story returns “unverified cache” and offers a second survey instead of conjuring stock.

### Field 05 expansion — Ash-weather interpretation

Weather and NuclearWinterProgression provide the current phase, season, temperature, daylight, wind, precipitation, and seeded variation. Recovery content can describe how ash lies, lifts, freezes, or washes, but it cannot create a sixth season or a second forecast. The same observation may read differently in deep winter and pale spring while retaining one owner result. This gives the prose room to change without changing the simulation contract.

### Field 06 expansion — Survivor witness roles

Witnesses can be resident, traveler, responder, child, archivist, or skeptic. SurvivorAutonomy and relationship owners provide traits, affinity, refusal, and availability. A witness may decline an interview, contradict a previous account, or ask that a name remain private. The plan stores the request and routes the decision to the archive or consent owner. It never uses dialogue choice as a hidden relationship mutation.

### Field 07 expansion — Repair-versus-retire decisions

Every damaged object scene offers a repair, repurpose, quarantine, or retirement framing. Construction, crafting, shelter, and inventory owners decide feasibility. Recovery can show the consequence of waiting, such as a route remaining narrow or a clinic missing a bench, but it cannot mark a building repaired before a project receipt arrives. A retired object can still become an archive source or memorial item.

### Field 08 expansion — Long-tail return cadence

The same scar can generate a first visit, a verification visit, a stewardship visit, and an anniversary visit. Cadence filters are keyed by location, source, and observation class. They prevent daily duplicate prompts while allowing a meaningful seasonal change to surface. The archive receives a stable event ID and a source list, making the long tail searchable rather than noisy.

### Field 09 expansion — Player-facing uncertainty language

The recovery panel uses three confidence labels: reported, observed, and confirmed by owner. “Reported” can be acted on only through a safe follow-up. “Observed” can support a low-risk plan. “Confirmed by owner” can unlock the route or project allowed by that owner. The labels are keyboard-focusable, read aloud through the accessibility cue path, and retained in the journal so a player can understand why a decision was deferred.

### Field 10 expansion — Closure and re-opening

A scar card closes when its stated evidence, owner receipt, and player decision are complete. It can reopen only when a new owner event changes the premise: weather closure, fresh disaster, route damage, resident request, or archive correction. A reopened card does not duplicate the old reward. It shows the new delta, links to the earlier record, and asks for a new decision. This creates continuity without an infinite quest loop.

## Pass 46 — Recovery crew progression, training, and noncombat mastery

This pass gives repeated recovery work a readable progression. Mastery is a projection of education, autonomy, equipment, and completed owner receipts. It does not become a second skill tree or an invisible numerical advantage.

### Field 01 expansion — Crew profile

A crew profile contains stable survivor IDs, role preferences, known restrictions, and recent assignments. Roster and autonomy owners remain authoritative. Recovery only requests a crew shape, such as two observers and one carrier. The assignment response can accept, refuse, substitute, or defer. Each result is visible in the plan preview before departure.

### Field 02 expansion — Training cards

Training cards teach one safe practice at a time: mark a route, label a sample, preserve a witness account, pack a mask, or close a camp. SurvivorEducation supplies subject progress and teacher availability. A card can be completed by demonstration, supervised work, or reading. It unlocks better prompts and fewer mistakes, not an untracked bonus to every future expedition.

### Field 03 expansion — Mentor continuity

A mentor can accompany the same learner across a short chain of jobs. The relationship owner supplies affinity and availability; the recovery plan stores only the chain ID and lesson receipt. If the mentor refuses, is ill, or is assigned elsewhere, the lesson can pause without failing the campaign. A different qualified teacher can resume from the recorded lesson state.

### Field 04 expansion — Equipment literacy

Recovery content names equipment through inventory IDs: mask, sample jar, line marker, camera, radio, tarp, or thermal probe. The item owner reports quantity and condition. A learner can practice with a damaged item only when the owner permits it. The panel tells the player which equipment is missing and which substitution is safe; it never treats text flavor as possession.

### Field 05 expansion — Quality review

Completed jobs enter a review queue. A reviewer checks source, owner receipt, route status, and closure language. Reviews can pass, request correction, or escalate to a specialist. Archive, cartography, and disaster owners receive only the facts relevant to them. A rejected report remains useful as a training example and does not vanish from the journal.

### Field 06 expansion — Fatigue and humane pacing

Crew pacing reads needs, health, weather, route, and recent work from existing systems. The plan can recommend a rest, shorter route, or handoff. It cannot deduct fatigue itself. When the owner returns a fatigue or health constraint, the recovery panel explains the blocked choice and offers a safe alternative. This keeps humane pacing playable without duplicating needs math.

### Field 07 expansion — Community certification

A shelter or outpost can recognize a completed competency with an archive note or celebration moment. Certification is a record of evidence, not a global permission. A certified observer still needs the right tool and route. The record can support later dialogue, teaching, or assignment matching while remaining stable across saves.

### Field 08 expansion — Failure learning

A failed job records the exact failure class: missing evidence, unsafe weather, route closure, equipment mismatch, consent refusal, or owner timeout. The next training card references that class. The player sees a correction path rather than a generic “mission failed.” Repeating a failure without a new attempt is suppressed by cadence rules.

### Field 09 expansion — Crew composition stories

Small stories emerge from role combinations: a careful recorder with an impatient driver, two witnesses who disagree, or a learner who knows the ground better than the mentor. These scenes use relationship and autonomy responses. They can change who volunteers for a future job only through the existing relationship/action seam. The prose remains optional and skippable.

### Field 10 expansion — Mastery review

At a milestone, the plan summarizes work completed, evidence quality, safety decisions, lessons, and unresolved questions. A player can archive the review, assign a follow-up, or leave it open. The summary is deterministic and save-safe because it is built from recorded receipts, not random praise or hidden counters.

## Pass 47 — Recovery release gates, replayability, and archival aftercare

The final pass for this turn makes the expansion practical to implement in thin slices. It binds content volume to deterministic records, bounded UI work, and evidence that a player can recover from interruption.

### Field 01 expansion — Slice selection

The first slice uses one burn scar, one survivor witness, one route question, one sample request, one archive candidate, and one return receipt. It proves the owner chain without requiring a world-wide fire model. Additional slices add only one new owner seam at a time.

### Field 02 expansion — Seeded replay

All choice results that vary by seed use the current deterministic RNG contract. A replay records the seed, owner inputs, and selected card IDs. A same-seed run must produce the same assignment, evidence order, and closure labels. A different seed may choose a different witness or weather description while preserving owner boundaries.

### Field 03 expansion — Save interruption

The slice is interrupted before departure, during evidence review, after a refusal, and after return. Reload must preserve the open card, owner receipts, privacy setting, and next action. A receipt is idempotent; loading twice cannot duplicate an archive entry, item delivery, or notification.

### Field 04 expansion — Accessibility gate

Every decision has a visible label, focus order, keyboard/controller action, and text equivalent for audio. Quiet mode suppresses duplicate recovery cues while leaving critical alerts available through the AudioAccessibilityCoordinator path. The panel exposes why a button is disabled rather than relying on color or sound.

### Field 05 expansion — Performance gate

The recovery board loads metadata first, limits detailed rows to the selected card, and unsubscribes when hidden. It does not scan every location or survivor each frame. A stress fixture with 200 cards must remain responsive because filters operate on indexed metadata and owner queries are bounded.

### Field 06 expansion — Content lint

Every card is checked for stable ID, owner, source, action, failure, closure, accessibility label, and save behavior. A card that names an unsupported mechanic fails lint with a direct correction. This lets writers contribute high volume without smuggling a second ledger into prose.

### Field 07 expansion — Archive aftercare

Closed cards receive a source list and a short aftercare prompt. The prompt can invite a memorial, a future survey, or no further action. Aftercare is not a hidden reward; it is a transparent choice that can be revisited through the archive search.

### Field 08 expansion — Rollback behavior

If a content batch is rolled back, open cards are marked unavailable with a migration note. Existing owner state remains untouched. The player can finish unrelated work and the journal explains that the card will return when its package is enabled. No save section is deleted to make a content rollback appear clean.

### Field 09 expansion — Telemetry without surveillance

Development diagnostics count card opens, owner timeouts, duplicate receipts, and accessibility failures. They do not record private witness text or player identity. Release builds keep only the player-facing journal and the minimum error message needed to recover.

### Field 10 expansion — Definition of done

A recovery expansion slice is complete when one route can be discovered, staffed, executed, interrupted, reloaded, reviewed, archived, and replayed with the same seed. It is not complete because a large list of prose cards exists. The same gate applies to later scar regions and long-tail aftercare.

## Pass 48 — Recovery operations runbook, live evidence, and post-release stewardship

This pass closes the current expansion wave with an operator-facing runbook. It describes how a recovery feature stays truthful after release when weather shifts, packages change, players reload old saves, and communities continue living with the scar.

### Field 01 expansion — Daily evidence sweep

A daily sweep reads only owner events that can affect open recovery cards: route changes, weather shifts, disaster status, new archive sources, communications notices, vehicle changes, and survivor availability. The sweep emits a bounded list of changed premises. It does not rescan every location, recompute fire state, or mutate cards in place. A player sees which premise changed and can choose whether to reopen the card.

### Field 02 expansion — Operator triage

Development tools group failures by missing owner response, duplicate receipt, invalid catalog ID, save mismatch, accessibility regression, or stale content. The group includes card ID, owner, version, and recovery suggestion. Private witness text is excluded. This makes a large content bank supportable without turning diagnostics into a second archive.

### Field 03 expansion — Safe live copy

When a weather or route fact changes after a card was written, the runtime uses a short, neutral update: “The earlier route note is stale; the expedition owner now reports a closure.” The original copy remains in the journal. The update names the source and the next safe action, avoiding dramatic claims that the simulation cannot support.

### Field 04 expansion — Player trust repair

If a card displayed an incorrect owner result, the recovery UI offers a visible correction entry. The entry says what was wrong, which owner now governs, and whether the player’s prior decision remains valid. If a reward or item was duplicated, the owning ledger resolves it; recovery records the correction receipt and does not invent a compensating currency.

### Field 05 expansion — Old-save migration

A save made before a content batch can contain an open location reference, archived report, or completed recovery flag that the new package does not recognize. Migration maps stable IDs, marks unknown references as legacy, and preserves the player journal. The player receives a short explanation and a valid next action. No old save is rewritten into a new fire model.

### Field 06 expansion — Regional staffing

When the player’s primary shelter lacks a qualified crew, recovery can query another shelter, colony, or outpost through existing route and communications owners. The runbook defines the response for available, delayed, unreachable, and refused support. A remote crew never appears until a route, message, and assignment receipt exists.

### Field 07 expansion — Quiet-mode policy

Routine ash observations, archive updates, and training completions can be coalesced. Fire or route emergencies use the critical cue list and visual fallback. The policy records the requested coalescing interval and verifies that a quiet player still receives a readable event history. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator remains the sole presentation authority.

### Field 08 expansion — Archive retention

Recovery records have a source, confidence, owner, and retention class. A temporary field note can expire from the active board while remaining searchable in the archive. A memorial or public record requires the archive and consent paths. Retention is a record policy, not a reason to duplicate the save state in the recovery plan.

### Field 09 expansion — Content batch cadence

New cards arrive in small batches grouped by owner seam and region. Each batch includes fixture responses, accessibility strings, rollback notes, and a known limitation list. Writers can continue drafting future cards in a quarantine package while integrators verify the previous batch. The cadence supports high volume without flooding the live board.

### Field 10 expansion — Stewardship review

At the end of a release window, reviewers ask whether the burn scar remains legible, whether uncertainty is explained, whether refusals are respected, whether owner receipts are visible, and whether the player can recover from interruption. A “needs evidence” result is a useful outcome and creates the next bounded review task.

### Pass 48 operational acceptance sequence

1. Select one open recovery card and record its stable ID, owner list, confidence labels, and next action.
2. Advance one owner premise, such as a route closure or weather shift, and confirm that the card reopens once with a linked reason.
3. Interrupt before the player chooses, reload, and verify that the same card and source list return.
4. Complete the safe action, capture the owner receipt, and verify that repeated refresh does not duplicate it.
5. Toggle quiet mode and controller navigation, then confirm that the visual alert and focus path remain usable.
6. Disable the content batch in a fixture save and confirm a migration note with owner state intact.
7. Re-enable the batch and confirm stable reconnection without changing the archived source.
8. Run the same seed twice and compare branch, assignment, and closure records.
9. Review the diagnostic bundle for secrets, private witness text, and unbounded polling.
10. Sign the batch only when the owner chain, save path, accessibility path, rollback path, and archive path are all evidenced.

## Pass 49 — Regional recovery relay, equitable access, and continuity under outage

This pass expands recovery where the closest safe route, radio, vehicle, or skilled responder is not the one nearest the player. It uses the existing region, communications, colony, expedition, survivor, archive, and accessibility owners and records the reason for each handoff.

### Field 01 expansion — Region relay

A recovery request can be offered to a neighboring region when the local owner returns unavailable or delayed. Cartography and route owners supply the region and travel facts. The relay response is available, delayed, unreachable, or refused. The recovery board displays the owner chain rather than pretending the regions share a mutable queue.

### Field 02 expansion — Low-bandwidth card

If a relay cannot carry photographs or long notes, communications returns a compact packet of stable IDs, confidence labels, and requested measurements. The player can approve a text-only handoff. When the full record arrives, archive and cartography owners decide whether it supersedes the compact note.

### Field 03 expansion — Mobility access

The recovery panel offers a route question, vehicle request, remote witness, or delayed visit when a survivor cannot reach a site. Vehicle, expedition, needs, and autonomy owners decide what is safe. Mobility access is a choice in the content, not a hidden penalty attached to a person.

### Field 04 expansion — Language and literacy support

A witness may request a teacher, interpreter, visual map, or private written exchange. Education, communications, and UI owners provide the supported route. The recovery card includes a plain-language summary and preserves the source wording when permission allows.

### Field 05 expansion — Safe public summary

A regional relay can publish an aggregate summary: sites checked, routes open, supplies requested, and questions unresolved. Archive and communications owners control the record. The summary never exposes a witness’s private account simply because the recovery operation crossed a boundary.

### Field 06 expansion — Outage queue

When a relay, archive, or map service is unavailable, cards remain in a bounded outage queue with last-known owner time. The queue offers retry, courier, local note, or wait. It does not poll continuously or convert an outage into a new resource system.

### Field 07 expansion — Return acknowledgement

A receiving region acknowledges the request, the evidence, and the expected next update. A missing acknowledgment remains visible. Recovery can close its local scene only when the receiving owner supplies a receipt or the player chooses to stop waiting.

### Field 08 expansion — Reciprocity record

A relay may ask the originating region for a map copy, sample, labor exchange, or archive source. Each request routes through its current owner. Reciprocity is shown as a relationship between requests, not a new regional currency.

### Field 09 expansion — Disagreement across regions

Two regions can return different route or witness reports. The card presents both sources, timestamps, and safe options. Archive and cartography owners may request a verification survey. Recovery never picks a winner silently.

### Field 10 expansion — Relay closure

A relay closes when the request is acknowledged, answered, declined, or intentionally withdrawn. The closure links both regional records and remains searchable after the active card disappears. A new owner event can reopen the same chain without duplicating the original action.

### Pass 49 relay acceptance sequence

1. Open a local recovery card and request a neighboring-region relay.
2. Run available, delayed, unreachable, and refused fixtures.
3. Confirm compact packet, privacy scope, source timestamp, and expected acknowledgment.
4. Interrupt during outage and reload without duplicating the request.
5. Complete the handoff, publish an aggregate summary, and verify linked regional records.
6. Reopen after a new owner event and confirm the old receipt remains intact.
7. Repeat with controller, quiet mode, and a same-seed replay.
8. Sign only when mobility, language, privacy, outage, and archive paths are all visible.

## Pass 50 — Recovery stewardship checklist and field handoff cards

This closeout packet turns the current recovery expansion into small reviewable cards.

### Field 01 — Source first
Every card begins with a source owner, source time, confidence, and stable location. Unknown values remain unknown until an owner answers.

### Field 02 — Safe action
The first offered action is reversible and low risk. A hazardous or irreversible action names its owner requirement and disabled reason.

### Field 03 — Crew consent
Crew assignment shows accept, refuse, substitute, and defer. Refusal routes to roster/autonomy and does not mutate recovery state.

### Field 04 — Tool truth
Tools are queried from inventory with condition and reservation. A descriptive line cannot grant an item.

### Field 05 — Route truth
Routes come from expedition, vehicle, weather, cartography, and disaster owners. A recovery card cannot open a route by itself.

### Field 06 — Memory choice
Witnesses and memorials use consent and archive choices. Public, private, and no-record outcomes remain distinct.

### Field 07 — Accessible cue
Every emergency and closure has visual, text, focus, and quiet-mode behavior through shared seams.

### Field 08 — Save point
Open card, owner receipt, privacy scope, next action, and closure key survive interruption and reload.

### Field 09 — Replay key
Same seed and same owner fixtures produce the same assignment, branch, and receipt order. Variation is bounded and explained.

### Field 10 — Handoff note
The final card lists untouched shared paths, known limitations, rollback behavior, and the next owner review.
